en:
【Jinxin Chapter, Part Two】

Mencius said, "How unkind was King Hui of Liang! A kind man extends his love from those he loves to those he does not love. An unkind man extends his disregard from those he does not love to those he loves." Gongsun Chou asked, "What do you mean?"
"King Hui of Liang, for the sake of land, caused his people to be ground to pieces and fought a war, suffering a great defeat. When he was about to renew the fight, fearing he could not win, he drove his beloved sons and younger brothers to die for it. This is what is meant by extending his disregard from those he does not love to those he loves."
Mencius said, "In the Spring and Autumn period, there were no righteous wars. Some were better than others, that is all. A punitive expedition is when the superior attacks the inferior. Enemy states do not launch punitive expeditions against each other."
Mencius said, "It is better to have no books than to believe everything in books. In the case of the 'Wucheng' chapter, I take only two or three strips of bamboo. A benevolent man is invincible in the world. When the most benevolent attacks the most unbenevolent, how could the blood have flowed so as to float pestles?"
Mencius said, "There are men who say, 'I am skilled at deploying troops; I am skilled at warfare.' This is a great crime. If a ruler loves benevolence, he will be invincible in the world. When he marched south, the northern barbarians complained; when he marched east, the western barbarians complained, saying, 'Why does he put us last?' When King Wu attacked Yin, he had three hundred war chariots and three thousand fierce warriors. The king said, 'Do not fear. I bring you peace, not war against the people.' They bowed their heads till their horns touched the ground, and kowtowed. The word 'expedition' means 'to correct.' Each desires to correct himself. What need is there for war?"
Mencius said, "A carpenter or wheelwright can give others the compass and square, but he cannot make them skillful."
Mencius said, "When Shun ate parched grain and wild herbs, it was as if he would do so for life. When he became emperor, wearing embroidered robes, playing the lute, with the two princesses serving him, it was as if it had always been so."
Mencius said, "Only now do I understand the gravity of killing a man's kin. If you kill a man's father, he will kill your father; if you kill a man's elder brother, he will kill your elder brother. So it is not that you kill yourself, but it is as close as a hair's breadth."
Mencius said, "In ancient times, passes were established to guard against violence; nowadays, passes are established to perpetrate violence."
Mencius said, "If a man does not practice the Way himself, it will not be practiced by his wife and children. If he employs others not according to the Way, he cannot employ his wife and children."
Mencius said, "He who is thorough in profit will not be destroyed in a bad year. He who is thorough in virtue will not be disordered in an evil age."
Mencius said, "A man who loves fame can yield a state of a thousand chariots. If he is not such a man, the look on his face will betray him over a single basket of rice or a bowl of soup."
Mencius said, "If the benevolent and worthy are not trusted, the state will be empty. Without ritual and righteousness, superiors and inferiors will be in disorder. Without government affairs, resources will be insufficient."
Mencius said, "There are cases where an unkind man gains a state. But there has never been a case where an unkind man gains the world."
Mencius said, "The people are the most important; the altars of the grain and soil come next; the ruler is the least important. Therefore, gaining the common people, one becomes emperor; gaining the emperor's favor, one becomes a feudal lord; gaining a feudal lord's favor, one becomes a high official. If a feudal lord endangers the altars of the grain and soil, he is replaced. When the sacrificial animals have been prepared, the grain offerings have been purified, and the sacrifices are offered at the proper times, yet there is drought or flood, then the altars of the grain and soil are replaced."
Mencius said, "Sages are teachers for a hundred generations. Such were Boyi and Liuxia Hui. Therefore, those who hear of the ways of Boyi become incorruptible though they were greedy, and resolute though they were cowardly. Those who hear of the ways of Liuxia Hui become generous though they were mean, and broad-minded though they were narrow. They rose up a hundred generations ago, and a hundred generations later, those who hear of them are all stirred to action. Could anyone but a sage have such an effect? How much more so those who personally received their instruction?"
Mencius said, "Benevolence is the distinguishing characteristic of man. When embodied in man's conduct, it is called the Way."

zh:
游侠，见字如面。
前些时日，老朽随府尹大人巡查蒙学，见学堂里的娃娃们一个个正襟危坐，埋首书卷，连我等走近了都未曾察觉。
老朽心下好奇，是何等妙文，能让这些上蹿下跳的娃娃们如此专心？一问才知，他们手中所读，竟是你前些时日所赠。
老朽又问，这些书好在何处？娃娃们七嘴八舌，老朽这才知道，原来你竟为每个孩子都择了不同的书，实在是费心了。而听闻老朽与你相熟，他们都央着我，定要代他们向你道声谢。
只是，真要问他们想说什么，这群小家伙却面露羞赧，讷讷而止了。最后，老朽想了个法子，让他们把想说的话都诉诸笔端，一并封在信里了。至于写了什么，老朽绝未偷看！
对了，娃娃们还托我转交几幅画作，说是读了书卷后的有感而发。他们都说，游侠你是他们见过最有眼光的人，定能欣赏他们的大作。
哈哈，看来往后若再有与孩子们打交道的差事，找游侠准是没错了。

en:
Dear Wanderer,

The other day, I accompanied the Prefect on an inspection of the village school. The children sat straight at their desks, noses buried in scrolls, so absorbed they didn't even notice us draw near.
Curious what could hold their attention so completely, I asked. Turns out, they were reading the very books you gifted them not long ago.
I inquired further: what made these books so special? The little ones burst into chatter, and that's when I learned you had chosen a different book for each child. What thoughtfulness.
When they heard I knew you, they begged me to pass along their thanks.
But when I asked what they wanted to say, shyness took over, and words failed them. So I suggested they write it down instead. Their letters are enclosed. And no, I did not peek!
Oh, and they also asked me to send you a few drawings. Inspired, they said, by your books. They all agreed you're the most discerning person they've ever met, and that you'd surely appreciate their masterpieces.
Seems to me, whenever there's a task involving children, you're the one to call.

en:
Liu Yuxi (Tang Dynasty)
A mountain needn't be high; it is famous so long as there is a deity on it. A lake needn't be deep; it has supernatural power so long as there is a dragon in it. My home is humble, but it enjoys the fame of virtue so long as I am living in it. The moss creeping onto the doorsteps turns them green. The color of the grass reflected through the bamboo curtains turns the room blue. Erudite scholars come in good spirits to talk with me, and among my guests there is no unlearned common man. In this humble room, I can enjoy playing my plainly decorated qin, or read the Buddhist Scriptures quietly, without the disturbance of the noisy that jar on the ears, or the solemn burden of reading official documents. My humble home is like the thatched hut of Zhuge Liang of Nanyang, or the Pavilion Ziyun of Xishu. Confucius once said, "How could we call a room humble as long as there is a virtuous man in it?"

zh:
"博浪张氏，瓠子堤成，白马投璧，世世镇河，诏为河伯。

年轻的时候，张彦霖不信命。命是枷锁，从婴孩时便将人的脊背和头颅锁在了土地上，动弹不得。打小，张彦霖就艳羡话本里的大侠。他们策马江湖，快意恩仇；他们来去如风，从无影踪。他们不用整日对着瓠子金堤学“七星埽绳”，也不用成日被关在家里，逐字句背《水部式》，更不用在幽殿之下，踩着森森白骨，去驯化……属于张家的“龙”。

这就是命么？张彦霖一边想着，一边去瓦肆，挑了一匹上好的白马。他要逃，逃去大漠孤烟直的塞北、逃去春水绿如蓝的江南，逃离如脉搏般扎入河洛的黄河，逃离一切被注定的命运。

南方的桃花开得旺，黄河边从没有过这些。张彦霖驾着马，却同一位风尘仆仆的绿衣女子擦肩而过。他还她不小心落下的帷帽，她赠他亲手炼出的丹药。

“这是什么药？”
“救命的药。”
“姑娘，你炼了这么多，要救的是什么人？”
“救，开封一城之人。”

所谓命运，总是当你想逃离时，便会趁机抓住你。
en:
The Zhang clan of Roaring Sands built the Gourd Dike, offered white horses and jade to the river, and for generations tamed the waters by imperial decree, they became the River Master.

Young Zhang Yanling never believed in fate. To him, fate was a yoke, locking a man's spine and skull to the earth from infancy, leaving him no room to struggle. As a boy, he envied the heroes from storytellers' tales, those who rode through Jianghu with unbridled freedom, who came and went like the wind, leaving no trace. They never had to spend their days studying "Seven-Star Levee Ropes" by the Gourd Dike, nor memorize the Water Administration Code word by word under lock and key. And they certainly didn't have to descend into shadowed halls, treading on bleached bones, to tame... the dragon of Zhang clan.

Was this really fate? With that thought, Zhang Yanling went to the marketplace and picked out a fine white horse. He would flee to the desert's lone smoke in the far north, to the spring waters greener than indigo in Jiangnan. He would escape the Yellow River, whose veins dug deep into the heartlands, and every last trace of his predestined life.

The peach blossoms of the south bloomed fiercely, nothing like the barren banks of the Yellow River. But as Zhang Yanling rode, he brushed shoulders with a travel-worn woman in green. He returned the hat she'd dropped; she gifted him a pill she'd refined herself.
"What kind of medicine is this?"
"The life-saving kind."
"You've made so many. Who are you saving?"
"An entire city. Kaifeng."

Fate, it seemed, always seized you the moment you tried to run.
Version 2.0 Travels in Strange Lands

zh:
习题一：九流门和孤云的弟子正在官财坊赌骰。
他们将各使用2枚正常情况点数为1-6的骰子。若两个骰子点数和一样为平局，请问他们平局的几率为多少？
答曰：1/36几率平局，因为机智的九流门弟子一般掏出两枚定制点数为6的骰子点数必为12；而孤云弟子只会老老实实投掷出2-12点数。因此，36种对局可能中，唯有孤云掷出两枚6点时才能平局。

习题二：正值茶季，醉花阴连日开设清饮茶宴。茶宴期间，樊楼每日为花间客随机斟来1种茶品，为径山茶、渠江薄片、仙崖石花中其一。
每日约有4成机率遇径山茶，3成机率品到渠江薄片，3成机率饮得仙崖石花。花间客于其间赌茗，出题如下：预期平均来上几日，方可品鉴全3种茶水？
答曰：通过简单证明，显而易见可得预期为5.6。但是，可以易容混入樊楼伙房1天品完。
en:
Exercise 1: Disciples from Nine Mortal Ways and Lone Cloud are gambling with dice at the market.
Each uses two regular dice (numbers 1–6). If their sums are equal, it's a tie. What's the probability of a tie?
Answer: 1 in 36. Why? The clever Nine Mortal Ways disciple brings two dice that always roll 6, totaling 12, while the Lone Cloud disciple rolls honestly, getting any sum from 2 to 12. Out of 36 possible combinations, only double sixes from Lone Cloud Disciples can tie, so 1/36.

Exercise 2: During tea season, Velvet Shade hosts daily tea tastings. Each day, guests are served one of three teas at Revelry Hall: Jing Mountain, Qujiang Thin Slice, or Xianya Stone Flower.
The chances are: 40% for Jing Mountain, 30% each for Qujiang Thin Slice and Xianya Stone Flower. So, how many days, on average, would it take for a guest to taste all three?
Answer: Simple calculation shows it's about 5.6 days. But, of course, you could always sneak into the kitchen of Revelry Hall and try them all in one go.

zh:
“咱鬼樊楼抓来了个新人？”
“人？那玩意能叫做人？”
“就是个狼养大的稀罕货，烈得很，昨儿耍了好大威风，抓了不知道几块皮走，还不是灌了药，关狗笼子里去了！”
“你是没听着，这被狼养大的玩意，疼起来叫得和人也不一样，倒是新鲜。”
只是她喊错了地方。
啧，莫说是狼的求救，这些人便连人的求救也听不懂，何况是兽呢。

月光挤进窗的瞬间，她弓着背，口中发出低沉的嚎叫，盯着那一缕稀薄的月色，向着狗笼撞去，一遍又一遍，笼子上干涸的血迹之上，再次被撞上新鲜的血迹和泪水。
曾经为人的短暂记忆，早已被狼群收养的漫长时间搓揉得模糊，她只记得一轮又一轮的月亮。
从郑家逃走，慌不择路撞入狼群时，那个夜晚天上的圆月。
和狼群一同生活，相互依偎，度过的无数个月亮。
这个人的地方，她很害怕，她想要回到她的月下去。

直到日复一日，驯化不成狗的狼，最终成为人的食物，被撕咬殆尽，丢弃在一旁。
撞碎牢笼的白狼主，看向那一轮月亮，像极了从郑家逃走时的那一轮月亮，她如同归家一般奔向狼群，发出委屈的嚎叫，月光洒在她遍布疤痕的脊背之上。
这世间，人将她当作狗，而狼将她当作狼。
en:
"Did Ghost Revelry Hall catch a new one?"
"A person? Can that thing be called a person?"
"It's just a rare creature raised by wolves, fierce indeed. It made a big scene yesterday, took who knows how many skins, but we drugged it and locked it in a dog cage!"
"You should've heard it—when this wolf-raised thing hurts, it doesn't cry like a person. Quite novel."
But she was crying for help in the wrong place.
Tch. These people wouldn't understand a human's cry for help, let alone a beast's.

The moment moonlight squeezed through the window, she arched her back, let out a low growl, and stared at that faint strand of moonlight, throwing herself against the dog cage—over and over. Fresh blood and tears stained the dried blood on the cage.
The brief memories of once being human had long been blurred by her years with the wolf pack. She only remembered moon after moon.
The full moon in the sky was the night she fled the Zheng family and stumbled into the wolf pack.
Countless moons spent living with the wolves, huddling together for warmth.
This human place terrified her; she wanted to return to her moon.

Day after day, a wolf that couldn't be tamed into a dog eventually became human food, torn apart and discarded.
The Wolf Maiden, having shattered the cage, looked up at the moon—it looked just like the moon the night she fled the Zheng family. She ran toward the wolf pack as if returning home, letting out a plaintive howl. Moonlight spilled over her scar-covered back.
In this world, humans saw her as a dog, but wolves saw her as a wolf.

Now, things have changed and people are gone; the wind sweeps the wilderness, the moonlight traces the doors, and the night at the shrine is hushed and solemn. The general bled to bring this peace, and now he's barred from ever tasting it. Entering the General's Shrine once more, you only wish...

You bow solemnly, just as Uncle Jiang asked of you many years ago. You witnessed that story unfold across Qinghe, and unknowingly became a part of it yourself. The general fighting to the death in blood-stained armor; this is loyalty. The warrior casting aside his name and riding north in disguise; this is righteousness. zh:
木头是角门里新来的狗，可它一来就发现这地方怪怪的，因为这灰坑的角落里，会“长”出小孩来！而且“长”得可快了，有时刚瞧见个人经过，那儿就会多个小小的、裹着破布的小孩。
木头把这事儿报告给了金水门街的狗老大——大聪明。
大聪明却不相信，毕竟它见过的孩子都娇娇地养在院里，一个孩子跑出来，两个大人尾巴似的跟在身后，喂饭的喂饭，披衣的披衣。所以孩子怎么可能从灰坑里“长”出来？
直到木头带着大聪明来角门里逛了一圈儿，大聪明才承认，这世上竟真有凭空“长”孩子的怪事。
这下该怎么办呢？
看着小脸泛青的孩子，大聪明叼来了自己的小毯子，木头叼来了路上捡的竹编乌龟；见小孩没反应，大聪明叼来了肉骨头，木头叼来了自己最爱吃的菌子……可那张小嘴还是不吭声。
束爪无策的两只狗急得汪汪叫，却听到身后传来一声——
“吵死人了！叫什么叫……咦，这怎么有个小娃娃?!来人、快来人啊！”
en:
Woody is new to the Forsaken Quarter. But from the moment he arrives, he finds this place strange. In the corner by the Ash Pit, children grow! And they grow fast. Sometimes he spots someone passing by, and suddenly there's a small child wrapped in rags.
Woody reports this to Big Smart, the dog boss of Goldwater Street. Big Smart doesn't believe it. The children he knows are all pampered at home. If one runs out, two adults trail behind like tails, feeding and clothing them. How could children possibly grow from the Ash Pit?
Only when Woody takes Big Smart for a walk around the Forsaken Quarter does Big Smart finally admit that there really are places where children sprout from nowhere.
Now what?
Seeing a child with a bluish little face, Big Smart fetches his own small blanket. Woody brings a bamboo turtle he found on the road. The child doesn't react. Big Smart brings a meaty bone. Wood brings his favorite mushrooms. Still, those little lips stay sealed.
The two dogs, at their wits' end, start barking anxiously. Then they hear a voice behind them:
"What's all this noise?! Stop barking. Huh?! Where did this child come from?! Help! Someone, quick!"

zh:
蒙学馆的院子里，有一颗石榴树，每到开花时，诸葛先生都会亲手摘下树上的石榴花，作为学童们读书的嘉奖。孩子们都以能戴上诸葛先生的小红花为荣，每逢花开时，都争着找先生背书。
木先生夸他想得好办法，他摇摇头，只说自己师父当年也是这样做的。木闻莺笑道：“没想到林文元还有这般巧的心思。”诸葛笑了笑，没有反驳。
他说的师父，并非当今文津馆文元。林师父待他极好，但他所说的，其实是另一位师父，初入文津馆时，为他开蒙的师父。师父不止授其诗书经史、琴棋书画，还带他夏日听泉，春来观花。
等诸葛到了开始修习武艺的年纪，师父却被天下大事唤走了。临行前种下了这颗石榴树，告诉诸葛非非：“为师此去谋太平，事成之时，树当结实，子当登科。”
于是诸葛被托付给了林师父，诸葛与他虽无正式的师徒之名，实则为林险生入文津馆后教导的首名弟子。他对诸葛倾囊以授，诸葛学得很快，林险生所授武学，看一遍便能记住，看三遍便能使出。林险生惊叹于他的天赋，只是同样一套剑法，别人使出来或凌厉或飘逸，他使出来则如剑谱般标准，却无半点情绪在其中。
林险生知道，一个师父应该做的，并非只是传其诗书或武艺，还需传其道，解其惑，而这些，皆需诸葛真正的师父亲自来，自己无法越俎代庖。所以诸葛非非只是终日读书习武，在石榴树下等着师父回来的消息。
en:
In the courtyard of the Primary Hall stood a pomegranate tree. Whenever it bloomed, Master Zhuge would personally pluck the pomegranate blossoms from its branches to reward the schoolchildren for their studies. The children took great pride in wearing Master Zhuge's little red flowers. Thus, every time the blossoms opened, they would vie with one another to recite their lessons to him.
Master Mu praised him for devising such a clever method. He shook his head, only replying that his own master had done exactly the same in the past. Mu Wenying laughed: "I never expected the Literary Champion Lin to possess such a delicate mind." Zhuge merely smiled, offering no rebuttal.
The master he spoke of was not the current Grand Scholar, or Wenyuan, of the Inkbound Order. Master Lin treated him exceedingly well, but the one he referred to was actually another master, the one who had enlightened his youthful mind when he first entered the Inkbound Order. This master did not merely teach him poetry, history, the classics, and the four scholarly arts; he also led him to listen to the bubbling springs in summer, and to admire the blooming flowers in spring.
By the time Zhuge reached the age to begin practicing martial arts, his master was summoned away by the great affairs of the realm. Before departing, he planted this pomegranate tree, leaving Zhuge Feifei with a promise: "Your master leaves to seek peace for the world. When this endeavor succeeds, the tree shall bear fruit, and you shall achieve glory in the exams."
Thus, Zhuge was entrusted to Master Lin. Though they shared no formal title of master and disciple, Zhuge was, in truth, the first pupil Lin Xiansheng taught upon entering the Inkbound Order. Lin held nothing back in his teachings, and Zhuge learned rapidly. The martial arts Lin Xiansheng imparted, he could memorize after watching but once, and execute flawlessly after watching thrice.
Lin Xiansheng marveled at his talent. Yet, for the very same swordplay, others might perform it with fierce sharpness or ethereal grace; when Zhuge performed it, it was as perfectly standard as a sword manual, but utterly devoid of emotion.
Lin Xiansheng knew that what a master should do is not merely transmit poetry or martial arts; he must also impart the Great Way and dispel his confusion. These things required Zhuge's true master to accomplish in person; Lin could not overstep his bounds to usurp that role.
Therefore, Zhuge Feifei simply read books and practiced martial arts all day long, waiting quietly beneath the pomegranate tree for news of his master's return.
Luancheng - Universal Harmony 1

《汉书》有云，“骏马名骓。”骓，指毛色苍白相间。契丹铁蹄中有此纹理者，为乌骓。
《辽史·食货志》有云：“契丹旧俗，其富以马，其强以兵。纵马於野，弛兵於民。有事而战，彍骑介夫，卯命辰集。马逐水草，人仰湩酪，挽强射生，以给日用，糗粮刍茭，道在是矣。以是制胜，所向无前。”契丹为游牧民族，素有逐水草而牧马之习俗，自辽国建立，六院之下专设马群司，掌彰愍宫马群牧养蕃息之事。契丹战马素以耐劳善忍、勇猛稳健著称，故名“契丹铁蹄”。
契丹铁蹄体格较小，肢粗而短，蹄小而圆，蹄质坚实，不易裂缝，步伐敏捷，即便于崎岖山路亦如履平地。性沉稳，耐粗饲，易增膘，寿命长，可负重乘骑，为契丹辽国最常见的马种。
en:
The Book of Han notes, "The name Zhui is for fine horses." Zhui refers to a coat mottled with pale and dark colors. Khitan Iron Hooves with this pattern are called Wuzhui.
The History of Liao records, "In old Khitan custom, wealth lay in horses, and strength in arms. Horses roamed the wilds; soldiers worked in the mass. When war arose, armored riders and soldiers gathered at dawn by royal command. Horses were raised by nature; people relied on dairy. They hunted live prey to meet daily needs. Travel, supplies, and fodder all followed this way and were drawn from local resources. Victory came from it, unstoppable in battle." As nomads, the Khitan raise horses along rivers and pastures. With the founding of the Liao Dynasty, they established a dedicated Horse Herd Office under the Six Bureaus to manage the imperial herds of Zhangmin Palace. Khitan warhorses are famed for endurance, strength, and composure, earning the title "Khitan Iron Hooves."
Khitan Iron Hooves are compact in build, with short, sturdy limbs and small, round hooves that rarely crack. Nimble-footed, they move easily even across rugged terrain. Calm in nature, tolerant of rough feed, quick to gain weight, long-lived, and capable of carrying both riders and loads, they are the most common horse in the Liao dynasty.

zh: 古人用“虫”泛指一切动物，并把虫分为五类：禽为羽虫，兽为毛虫，龟为甲虫，鱼为鳞虫，人为倮虫。“大”有长、为首的意思。虎属毛虫类，是兽中之王。“大虫”也就是毛虫之首领，兽中之王的意思。
en: Chong literally means "insect," but in ancient times, the term "chong" was used more broadly to refer to all living creatures, which were classified into five types: birds as feathered chong, beasts as furred chong, turtles as shelled chong, fish as scaled chong, and humans as naked chong. The word "da" (big) denotes not only size but also prominence or leadership. The tiger, as a furred chong, was regarded as the king of beasts, and thus was called "Da Chong," meaning the chief among chong, or the king of all beasts.

时厥明，王乃大巡六师，明誓众士。
王曰：“呜呼！我西土君子，天有显道，厥类惟彰。今商王受狎侮五常，荒怠弗敬。自绝于天，结怨于民，斮朝涉之胫，剖贤人之心，作威杀戮，毒𤸵四海。崇信奸回，放黜师保，屏弃典刑，囚奴正士。郊社不修，宗庙不享，作奇技淫巧以悦妇人。上帝弗顺，祝降时丧。尔其孜孜，奉予一人，恭行天罚。
“古人有言曰：‘抚我则后，虐我则雠。’独夫受洪惟作威，乃汝世雠，树德务滋，除恶务本。肆予小子诞以尔众士，殄歼乃雠。尔众士其尚迪果毅，以登乃辟。功多有厚赏，不迪有显戮。
“呜呼！惟我文考若日月之照临，光于四方，显于西土。惟我有周诞受多方。予克受，非予武，惟朕文考无罪。受克予，非朕文考有罪，惟予小子无良。”
……
en:
【Book of Zhou · Great Declaration III】

At the break of that day, the king made a grand inspection of the six armies and solemnly declared his oath to all the troops.
The king said: "Alas! You noble men of our western lands, Heaven has its manifest Dao, and its principles are clearly revealed. Now Shou, the king of Shang, treats the Five Constant Virtues with contempt, being idle and disrespectful. He has cut himself off from Heaven and incurred the resentment of the people. He has severed the shins of those who wade at dawn and ripped out the hearts of the worthy. He exercises tyranny and slaughter, poisoning the four seas. He trusts and favors the wicked and perverse, banishes his teachers and guardians, casts aside the statutes and punishments, and imprisons and enslaves the upright. He neglects the sacrifices to Heaven and Earth and fails to honor the ancestral temple, devising cunning tricks and lewd artifices to please women. Heaven does not favor him, and has sent down this calamity of destruction. Do you, therefore, strive diligently to support me, one man, in reverently executing Heaven's punishment.
"The ancients had a saying: 'If one cherishes us, he is our sovereign; if one oppresses us, he is our enemy.' The Lone Tyrant Shou, in his great tyranny, has become the enemy of your generation. In planting virtue, one should strive for abundance; in eradicating evil, one must strike at the root. Therefore, I, a humble one, together with you, the multitude of warriors, shall utterly destroy your enemy. Let you, the warriors, advance with resolute courage to elevate your sovereign. Those who achieve great merit shall receive rich rewards; those who do not advance shall face public execution.
"Alas! My late father, King Wen, was like the shining of the sun and moon, illuminating the four quarters and manifesting his brilliance in the western lands. Indeed, our Zhou has grandly received the allegiance of many regions. If I conquer Shou, it is not due to my martial prowess, but because my late father, King Wen, was without fault. If Shou conquers me, it is not because my late father, King Wen, had any fault, but because I, a humble one, lack virtue."

zh:
【乡射礼第五】

乡射之礼。主人戒宾，宾出迎，再拜。主人答再拜，乃请。宾礼辞，许。主人再拜，宾答再拜。主人退；宾送，再拜。无介。
乃席宾，南面，东上。众宾之席，继而西。席主人于阼阶上，西面。尊于宾席之东，两壶，斯禁，左玄酒，皆加勺。篚在其南，东肆。设洗于阼阶东南，南北以堂深，东西当东荣。水在洗东，篚在洗西，南肆。县于洗东北，西面。乃张侯，下纲不及地武。不系左下纲，中掩束之。乏参侯道，居侯党之一，西五步。
羹定。主人朝服，乃速宾；宾朝服出迎，再拜；主人答再拜，退；宾送，再拜。宾及众宾遂从之。
及门，主人一相出迎于门外，再拜；宾答再拜。揖众宾。主人以宾揖，先入。宾厌众宾，众宾皆入门左，东面北上。宾少进，主人以宾三揖，皆行。及阶，三让，主人升一等，宾升。主人阼阶上当楣北面再拜，宾西阶上当楣北面答再拜。
主人坐取爵于上篚，以降。宾降。主人阼阶前西面坐奠爵，兴辞降。宾对。主人坐取爵，兴，适洗，南面坐奠爵于篚下，盥洗。宾进，东北面辞洗。主人坐奠爵于篚，兴对，宾反位。主人卒洗，壹揖，壹让，以宾升。宾西阶上北面拜洗。主人阼阶上北面奠爵，遂答拜，乃降。宾降，主人辞降，宾对。主人卒盥，壹揖壹让升；宾升，西阶上疑立。主人坐取爵，实之宾席之前，西北面献宾。宾西阶上北面拜，主人少退。宾进受爵于席前，复位。主人阼阶上拜送爵，宾少退。荐脯醢。宾升席，自西方。乃设折俎。主人阼阶东疑立。宾坐，左执爵，右祭脯醢，奠爵于荐西，兴取肺，坐，绝祭，尚左手，哜之，兴，加于俎，坐梲手，执爵，遂祭酒，兴，席末坐啐酒，降席，坐尊爵，拜，告旨，执爵兴。主人阼阶上答拜。宾西阶上北面坐卒爵，兴，坐奠爵，遂拜，执爵兴。主人阼阶上答拜。
宾以虚爵降。主人降。宾西阶前东面坐奠爵，兴，辞降；主人对。宾坐取爵，适洗，北面坐奠爵于篚下，兴，盥洗。主人阼阶之东，南面辞洗。宾坐奠爵于篚，兴对。主人反位。宾卒洗，揖让如初，升。主人拜洗，宾答拜，兴，降盥，如主人之礼。宾升，实爵主人之席前，东南面酢主人。主人阼阶上拜，宾少退。主人进受爵，复位，宾西阶上拜送爵。荐脯醢。主人升席自北方。乃设折俎。祭如宾礼，不告旨，自席前适阼阶上，北面坐卒爵，兴，坐奠爵，遂拜，执爵兴。宾西阶上北面答拜。主人坐奠爵于序端，阼阶上再拜崇酒，宾西阶上答再拜。
……
en:
【Village Archery Ceremony, Fifth】

In the village archery ceremony, the host warns the guest, and the guest comes out to greet him, bowing twice. The host returns the bow twice, then makes the request. The guest politely declines, then accepts. The host bows twice, and the guest returns the bow twice. The host withdraws; the guest sees him off, bowing twice. There is no intermediary.
Then a mat is laid for the guest, facing south, with the seat of honor on the east. The mats for the other guests are laid in succession to the west. A mat is laid for the host on the eastern steps, facing west. The wine vessels are placed to the east of the guest's mat, two pots, on a stand, with the dark wine on the left, both with ladles. The basket is to the south of them, oriented east-west. A washing basin is set up southeast of the eastern steps, its north-south position determined by the depth of the hall, and its east-west position aligned with the eastern eaves. Water is east of the basin, and the basket is west of the basin, oriented south-north. The bell frame is northeast of the basin, facing west. Then the target is set up, with the lower cord not touching the ground by the length of a foot. The lower left cord is not tied, but folded and bound in the middle. The waiting screen is set at a distance of three times the target's length from the target, on the west side of the target's flank, five paces to the west.
When the food is ready, the host, in court robes, goes to invite the guest; the guest, also in court robes, comes out to greet him, bowing twice; the host returns the bow twice and withdraws; the guest sees him off, bowing twice. The guest and the other guests then follow him.
Upon reaching the gate, the host, with one assistant, comes out to greet them outside the gate, bowing twice; the guest returns the bow twice. He bows to the other guests. The host, with the guest, bows and enters first. The guest gestures for the other guests to enter, and they all enter through the left side of the gate, facing east with the seat of honor on the north. The guest advances slightly, and the host, with the guest, exchanges three bows as they walk. Upon reaching the steps, they yield three times, the host ascends one step, and the guest ascends. The host, on the eastern steps, facing north under the ridge beam, bows twice, and the guest, on the western steps, facing north under the ridge beam, returns the bow twice.
The host sits down, takes the goblet from the upper basket, and descends. The guest descends. The host, in front of the eastern steps, facing west, sits down, places the goblet on the ground, rises, and declines the guest's descent. The guest responds. The host sits down, picks up the goblet, rises, goes to the washing basin, sits down facing south, places the goblet beneath the basket, and washes his hands and the goblet. The guest advances, facing northeast, and declines the washing. The host sits down, places the goblet in the basket, rises to respond, and the guest returns to his position. The host finishes washing, exchanges one bow and one yielding, and ascends with the guest. The guest, on the western steps, facing north, bows for the washing. The host, on the eastern steps, facing north, places the goblet down and returns the bow, then descends. The guest descends, the host declines the guest's descent, and the guest responds. The host finishes washing his hands, exchanges one bow and one yielding, and ascends; the guest ascends and stands still on the western steps. The host sits down, picks up the goblet, fills it in front of the guest's mat, and offers it to the guest, facing northwest. The guest, on the western steps, facing north, bows, and the host withdraws slightly. The guest advances, receives the goblet in front of the mat, and returns to his position. The host, on the eastern steps, bows as he sends off the goblet, and the guest withdraws slightly. Dried meat and pickled vegetables are presented. The guest ascends to his mat from the west side. Then the carved meat platter is set up. The host stands still east of the eastern steps. The guest sits down, holds the goblet in his left hand, and with his right hand offers the dried meat and pickled vegetables, places the goblet to the west of the offerings, rises to take the lung, sits down, tears it in sacrifice, holding it in his left hand, tastes it, rises, places it on the platter, sits down to wipe his hands, takes the goblet, and then offers the wine, rises, sits at the end of the mat to sip the wine, descends from the mat, sits down to set the goblet down, bows, announces that the wine is excellent, and rises holding the goblet. The host, on the eastern steps, returns the bow. The guest, on the western steps, facing north, sits down, drains the goblet, rises, sits down to set it down, then bows, and rises holding the goblet. The host, on the eastern steps, returns the bow.
The guest descends with the empty goblet. The host descends. The guest, in front of the western steps, facing east, sits down, places the goblet on the ground, rises, and declines the host's descent; the host responds. The guest sits down, picks up the goblet, goes to the washing basin, sits down facing north, places the goblet beneath the basket, rises, and washes his hands and the goblet. The host, east of the eastern steps, facing south, declines the washing. The guest sits down, places the goblet in the basket, rises to respond. The host returns to his position. The guest finishes washing, exchanges bows and yieldings as before, and ascends. The host bows for the washing, the guest returns the bow, rises, descends to wash his hands, following the host's ritual. The guest ascends, fills the goblet in front of the host's mat, and offers it to the host, facing southeast. The host, on the eastern steps, bows, and the guest withdraws slightly. The host advances, receives the goblet, returns to his position, and the guest, on the western steps, bows as he sends off the goblet. Dried meat and pickled vegetables are presented. The host ascends to his mat from the north side. Then the carved meat platter is set up. He offers sacrifices as in the guest's ritual, but does not announce that the wine is excellent. From in front of his mat, he goes to the eastern steps, sits down facing north, drains the goblet, rises, sits down to set it down, then bows, and rises holding the goblet. The guest, on the western steps, facing north, returns the bow. The host sits down, places the goblet at the end of the eastern corridor, and on the eastern steps bows twice to honor the wine, and the guest, on the western steps, returns the bow twice.

zh:
天下人都追逐舍利，可是，嘿嘿，追不到。
因为舍利是一只跑得很快的小猫。
一只猫跑得快有什么用呢？
舍利也不知道，但舍利正是靠着它的速度，从长安跑到凉州，又从山底跑上山顶。
雪下得好大。舍利窝在雪里，和雪一样白。
或许，跑得快是没用的，跑向哪儿才有用。合上眼前，舍利这么想。
睁开眼它在一个温暖的屋子里，火烧得劈啪作响，那个胡子拉碴的男人，把它带回了家。
从此，它不用再做一只跑得快的小猫。
en:
While everyone chases the swift little cat Relic, 
it remains just out of reach. 
What good is speed for a cat? 
Relic doesn't know, but it's speed that carried it from Chang'an to Liangzhou, from valley floor to mountaintop. 
Snow falls thick and soft. Relic curls into the white, blending with the flakes. 
Perhaps speed isn't what matters, but where you run to. Closing its eyes, Relic thinks this. 
When they open, it's in a warm room, fire crackling nearby. A scruffy man has brought it home. 
From that day on, Relic no longer needs to be the fastest cat.

zh: 《春秋穀梁传》成于战国至汉初。春秋三传之一，《春秋》经传初各单行，后人割传附经，遂成今本。相传为穀梁赤受学于子夏，口说流传，至汉初始著于竹帛。全书以阐释《春秋》义例为主，其文质朴，多设问答以明经义。尤重礼制与伦理。汉宣帝喜《穀梁》之学，召名儒于石渠阁论五经异同，亲称制临决，立《穀梁》博士，其学遂大行于世。东晋范宁作《春秋穀梁传集解》，兼采三家。唐杨士勋据范注作疏，题为《春秋穀梁传注疏》，列入官学，为九经之一。其学与《公羊》同重义理而各有侧重，《公羊》长于论政，《穀梁》精于明礼。
en: "Er" signifies nearness; "ya" signifies correctness. Together they form a vast sea of classical exegesis and a master key to the Six Arts. As recorded in the Book of Sui: Treatise on Classics, this work was once placed alongside "The Classic of Filial Piety," for its role in rectifying names and distinguishing things made it a fitting companion to the study of the classics. Scholars today regard it as the first rung on the ladder of classical learning and the vessel by which one crosses into antiquity. That it glosses "chu," "zai," "shou," and "ji" all under the single meaning of "beginning" is itself a testament to how one word may reveal the heart of a matter, drawing ten thousand things back to a single source, resolving for readers across all ages the great riddles left by the ancients.

zh:
大漠深处有一个小村庄，隐藏在月光最亮的沙谷中。
那里有一湾清泉，可以倒映出天光霁月，万里星河。而更神奇的是，水中的一轮月华可以被特殊的捞月网捕捉，变成松软香甜的白面馍馍。
那馍馍拿在手里轻飘飘，却散发着熨帖热气。吃上几口，只觉舌尖回甘幽香，腹中饥火霎时被熄灭。
靠着这神奇的月光馍馍，村里人过着衣食无忧的生活。
可这世上总有不被神佛垂青的芸芸苦众。沙海无垠，生存本就是一种苦难。连年的战火，更是榨干了那些渴望活着的灵魂。饿殍遍地，残骨累累。
诞生于乐境的少年不忍看到村子之外的人受饥饿之苦。他拿起所有能找到的捞月网，一步一步走出了清辉笼罩的故乡。
他想把馍馍的秘密享给那些苦命人。毕竟，月亮也不只是村里人的月亮。
en:
Deep in the desert was a small village, hidden in the sandy valley where the moonlight was brightest. 
There was a clear spring there that could reflect the sky's light, the clear moon, and the starry river spanning ten thousand miles. Even more wondrous, a disk of moonlight in the water could be caught with a special moon-catching net and transformed into soft, sweet white-flour buns. 
The buns felt light in the hand but emitted comforting warmth. After a few bites, a subtle, sweet fragrance lingered on the tongue, and the fire of hunger in the belly was instantly quenched. 
Relying on these miraculous moon-buns, the villagers lived a life free from want for food and clothing. 
But this world always has multitudes of suffering souls not favored by gods and Buddhas. The sea of sand is boundless; survival itself is a kind of hardship. Years of war further drained the souls of those desperate to live. Starved bodies littered the ground, piles of bleached bones. 
A boy born in this joyful realm couldn't bear to see people outside the village suffer from hunger. He took all the moon-catching nets he could find and, step by step, walked out of his homeland bathed in clear light. 
He wanted to share the secret of the buns with those less fortunate. After all, the moon wasn't just the moon of the villagers.

新章将启，燕渡重洋。山海无垠，侠心同归。
2025年11月15日，《燕云十六声》国际版正式上线，全球登陆。
十六声，非独为乐，千载文脉，声声相传，方铸侠心剑魂。
幸得千万游侠汇聚，天地众声相和，雏燕生出羽翼，飞越青云。

衷心祝愿海外运营团队长风破浪，与海外游侠共襄江湖之盛。
值此良辰，奉上置景【界碑·自远风】及谢礼一份，贺八方同心，答知遇之情。
四海纵侠气，万里可同风。
愿天下游侠都可在风起之地，循音相逢。
en:
Dear Wanderer,

A new chapter dawns.
On November 15, 2025, Where Winds Meet goes global.
Thanks to millions of wanderers, all sing in harmony. Young swallows spread their wings, soaring past azure clouds.
May the flickering torch of Eastern martial arts illuminate the four seas.
To our overseas team: may fair winds bear you onward, as you share this Jianghu with wanderers worldwide.
On this joyous occasion, we present the Decoration [Boundary Stone - Beyond the Winds] and a token of gratitude.
Xia courses will bring every one of us together.
May every wanderer at the place where wind rises find each other through song.

en:
To my young brother, 
   If you're reading this, then you know what has happened, and you likely have doubts in your heart. I thought about this for a long time and made up my mind. For many years, I blamed the death of Father Li on my adoptive father. Recently, through the master, I discovered that I had been harboring my hatred for the wrong person. Father Li was killed by a single phrase from the government: "When there are no more birds, the bow becomes useless." I had been in the wrong for many years and assisted the culprit. The kindness of my adoptive father and the revenge for Father Li... I bear both on my shoulders. 
   Only by destroying the ship can I put an end to this. Now I can go see Father Li. 
   Please fulfill my wish by stopping the hatred and not coming with me. Take care of yourself, and put on more clothes when the weather gets cold.

#G刀刃刺进那魑魅的胸膛，可却仿佛刺进了棉花一样。一阵金光闪过，桃小妹眼前哪有什么魑魅，只出现了两个兄长的身影，原来是此二人早已将那魑魅斩于剑下，此番不过是为戏弄小妹，才合力演了这出难辨真假的偶人戏。#E

>页六（近年的纸张，纸张有泪渍打湿的痕迹）
#G桃源三剑回到了桃源乡，因斩了那魑魅，外面的人们寻迹而来，桃源乡成了桃源城、又发展为桃源国。人们终日乐呵呵，不知饥馑，也从未见过战乱。#E
#G那桃源三剑呢？桃源三剑隐姓埋名，就像普通人家的兄妹一样，在桃源乡慢慢变老。纵然变成了三个牙齿都掉光了的老头老太，每天却仍还围在一起编话本，吵吵闹闹的，一人一段，像三个孩子一样……#E

落款：#R师#E#G晴#E#Y崖#E
en:
Page Five (paper of recent make)
#GThe blade sank into the Chimei's chest, yet it felt as though it had pierced cotton. A flash of golden light passed before Tao Xiaomei's eyes, and there was no Chimei at all, only her two brothers. It turned out the pair had long since cut the creature down. This whole business had only been a puppet show they staged together to tease their little sister, putting on a scene so convincing that truth and falsehood could scarcely be told apart.#E

Page Six (paper of recent make, stained with tears)
#GThe Three Swords returned to Haven. Because they had slain the Chimei, people from outside followed the trail there, and Haven became Haven City, then in time grew into the Kingdom of Haven. The people lived in cheer day after day, knowing neither hunger nor war.#E
#GAnd what became of the Three Swords of the Haven? They hid their names away and grew old in Haven like the siblings of any ordinary household. Even when they had turned into three toothless old folk, they still sat together every day making up storybooks, bickering all the while, each adding a part, carrying on just like three children...#E

zh:
问题一：
秋招拿下零个录选，我做对了什么！
自从听说宝慈宫要笑招，我日日对镜苦练笑话，可最终连秋姐姐的面都没见着。听说她只抽选了一批合眼缘的进入笑招，说运气也是实力的一部分……难怪大家都说秋招想要被录选，刚入宫这一年很关键，如果没有在第一年被秋姐姐记住，是不是这辈子都去不了宝慈宫了……可我真的很想说，今日我为娘子效力，明日娘子以我为荣！
答复一：
姐妹莫要气馁！刚入宫“榜上无名”未必是坏事。木秀于林，风必摧之，不如先韬光养晦，练好一门手艺才是硬道理！
答复二：
与其想着“让娘子以我为荣”，不如想着“怎么让娘子离不开我”。我当年就是死磕“双面绣”，如今连娘子的衣服破了都得等我补，尚功局的女史都替不了手……姐妹们一定得明确自己的核心竞争力！
答复三：
接接接！接好心态！其实没被选上也好，省得天天提心吊胆。咱们这种小宫人，平安熬到出宫便是最大的造化！（悄悄话：楼上的姐姐，我猜出你是谁了！你的针线活儿当真是一绝！）

分享一：
托尚食局好姐妹的福，竟尝到了主子们赏下来的“酥山”！虽然有些化了，但这滋味简直鲜掉眉毛！奶香浓郁，里头还有碎果仁！
呜呜呜，虽然只是边角余料，但为了这一口，我愿意再在宫里熬个五年！且吃且珍惜！
答一：
哈哈哈哈悄悄告诉你，下回馋了，趁着姐姐们歇了，来尚食后门找我！我给你留个“余料”最足的！
答二：
姐妹，这东西虽然好吃，但是寒气重！吃完记得喝碗姜汤暖暖胃，不然下次来月事可不好受！

问题二：
家人们谁懂啊，分到了冷宫值夜，这里阴森森的，晚上风吹得灯笼直晃，吓死我了。
刚入宫的妹妹们切莫贪睡，本以为能分到六尚学门手艺，结果误了卯，直接被发配到冷宫守夜！而且月例银子微薄，什么都买不起！有没有懂行的姐妹支个招，怎么才能调去尚食局？
答一：
若能像上头分享“酥山”那个姐妹般馋嘴……不，热爱美食，兴许能行！最要紧的是，你得让人能瞧出你能吃苦、有力气！尚食局看着光鲜，其实还要搬面粉、劈柴火呢！
答二：
想要来我们这儿？光有热情不够，得眼里有活儿！我们这儿缺的是对吃食有讲究的，你平日无事多去尚食后门帮着择菜、倒泔水，混个脸熟。上次有个小丫头就是帮我剥了三天蒜，我看她手脚麻利才把人要过来的。
答三：
调拨之事急不得，保重身子骨要紧！冷宫湿气重，记得去讨点艾草熏一熏，膝盖上一定要绑护膝！身子垮了，便什么都没了！

分享二：
看着宫外放的烟花，突然就哭了。进宫八年了，不知道阿爹阿娘身体怎么样，弟弟是不是长高了。
宫墙太高了，什么时候才能飞出去啊……
答一：
抱抱姐妹。我也八年了，刚进宫那会儿天天哭，如今泪都流干了。别怕，你看天上的月亮，咱们和爹娘瞧见的，是同一个呢。
答二：
……若是实在想家，下月初五我可能会去收炭火，你写封家书，偷偷塞进这本簿册里给我，我托那个送炭的老伯帮你带出去。切记，万不可让人瞧见！
答三：
偷偷说……遣散宫女的事好像下来了，想出宫的，这两日便可去寻尚宫大人探探口风！
en:
Question 1: How did I manage to get picked exactly zero times in the Autumn Selection?
Ever since I heard Baoci Palace was running a "Laughter Recruitment," I've been drilling jokes in day. And in the end, I didn't even get to see Sister Qiu.
They say she only let a handful of girls she liked the look of move on, and that "luck is part of strength"...
No wonder everyone says your first year matters most. If Sister Qiu doesn't remember you in year one, does that mean you're never getting into Baoci Palace, not ever?
Still. I really want to say it: I serve my lady today, and tomorrow my lady will be proud of me!

Reply 1:
Don't be so down. Being a nobody your first year isn't always a bad thing.
Stick your head out and you'll be the first to get clipped. Lie low for now and get a solid skill under your belt. That's what counts.

Reply 2:
Forget "make my lady proud." Think "make my lady unable to do without me."
I bet everything on double-sided embroidery back then. Now if my lady's robe so much as snags, it waits for my hands. Even the female clerks in the Crafts Office can't fill in.
Sisters, know your core advantage.

Reply 3:
You got this, you got this. Keep your head straight.
Honestly, not getting picked might be a blessing. At least you won't be on edge every day.
For small fry like us, making it safely to the day we leave is the best fortune there is.
(Whisper: sister upthread, I think I know who you are. Your stitching is insane.)

Share 1:
Bless my bestie in the Culinary Office, I finally got to try su shan from the nobles' leftovers!
It was a little melted, but the taste was unreal. Super creamy, with crushed nuts inside.
Even if it was just the scraps, I'd do five more years in here for a bite like that. Eat it while you can.

Reply 1:
Hahaha, secret for you. Next time you're craving it, come by the Culinary Office back gate when the senior sisters are resting.
I'll save you the tray with the biggest leftovers.

Reply 2:
It is tasty, but it's "cold" food. Drink some ginger soup after, warm your stomach.
Otherwise your next period is going to be rough.

Question 2:
Please tell me I'm not the only one. I got assigned to night watch at the Forlorn Palace.
It's creepy. The wind makes the lanterns swing all night. I'm terrified.
New girls, don't oversleep. I thought I'd get placed in one of the Six Offices to learn a skill, but I missed the Mao-hour roll call and got sent straight here.
And my monthly stipend is tiny. I can't afford anything. Any sisters who know the ropes, how do I transfer to the Culinary Office?

Reply 1:
If you're as "passionate" about food as the sister who posted about su shan... I mean, if you truly love food, you might have a shot.
Key thing is people need to see you can take hardship and do heavy work. The Culinary Office looks nice, but someone's still hauling flour sacks and chopping firewood.

Reply 2:
You want in? Enthusiasm isn't enough. You need to have an eye for work.
We need people who care about food. When you have time, go help out at the Culinary Office back gate. Pick vegetables, dump slop buckets, make yourself a familiar face.
Last time a little one peeled garlic for me three days straight. I only asked for her because her hands were quick and she didn't complain.

Reply 3:
Transfers take time. Take care of your health first.
The Forlorn Palace is damp. Go beg some mugwort and smoke the room a bit. And wrap your knees. If your body gives out, you've got nothing.

Share 2:
I saw fireworks outside the walls and just started crying.
Eight years in here. I don't know how my mother and father are doing, or if my little brother's grown taller.
These walls are too high. When do I ever get to fly out?

Reply 1:
Hang in there, sister. I'm eight years in too.
When I first came, I cried every day. Now I feel like I've run out of tears.
Look at the moon. It's the same one our parents are seeing.

Reply 2:
If you miss home that badly... on the fifth day next month, I might be going to collect charcoal.
Write a letter and slip it into this ledger for me. I'll ask the old man who delivers the charcoal to take it out.
Be careful. Don't let anyone see.

Reply 3:
Just between us, I heard the order to dismiss palace maids is coming down.
If you want out, go sound out the Registry Director in the next couple of days.

zh:
阿桂好战。

它原本是一窝幼犬里最羸弱的那只。但它护食，不放过任何能咽下肚的东西，更不放过任何敢来抢食的同类。凭借着这股不要命的狠劲，它成了那窝小狗里唯一活下来的。

然而仅凭好战与狠厉，终究抵不过漫天风雪。
隆冬的一天，它僵死般卧倒在山寺的门槛边。直到一双比落雪暖不了多少的手，轻轻将它捧起。

再次醒来时，它听到一阵“笃笃”声。循着木鱼声找去，声音戛然而止。
“师兄，想不到这小狗喝了点热菜汤竟能缓过来，我还以为……”
小沙弥惊喜地朝它走近。
它弓起背，喉咙里发出警惕的呜呜声。
“别动它，这狗在外面讨生活受过伤，不能随便碰。”另一个沉稳的声音拦住了小沙弥。

小狗好几次想溜下山，可每当它试探着迈出门槛，那两人总会适时地端来一碗热乎乎的菜汤，远远地放在台阶上。
不知不觉，大半年就这么过去了。

小沙弥一直琢磨着给它起个威风的名字，却被一位常来的香客抢了先。
香客笑着说，每回上山，这小黄狗总会在前头默默带路，不吠不叫，挺“寡言少语”的，和这清净的桂花庭院颇为相配。
“就叫阿桂吧！”

时逢秋暮，林间的桂花簌簌落在阿桂的背上。它抖了抖毛，对这些香得有些刺鼻的花瓣感到一丝苦恼。
天香桂子，白云叠叠。
阿桂打了个大大的喷嚏，趴在被阳光晒暖的青石板上，迷迷糊糊地想起——自己似乎已经很久，很久没有打过架了。
en:
Osmanthus loved a fight.

He was the runt of the litter. But he guarded his food fiercely. He ate anything he could get down, and fought any littermate who came for it. That reckless ferocity made him the only one to survive.

But fight and fury alone couldn't carry him through the snowstorm.
One day deep in winter, he lay frozen by the gate of a mountain temple, until a pair of hands, barely warmer than the falling snow, gently gathered him up.

When he woke up, he heard a rhythmic knocking. He followed the sound of the wooden fish, and the sound abruptly stopped.
"Brother, I never thought a bit of warm broth would bring him round. I was sure he'd..."
A young novice monk approached him, delighted.
Osmanthus arched his back and growled low in his throat.
"Leave him be. This dog has been hurt scraping a living out there. You don't reach for him carelessly." A steadier voice held the novice back.

The dog tried more than once to slip away down the mountain, but each time he ventured a paw past the gate, the two of them would appear with a bowl of steaming broth and set it down on the steps, some distance away.
Before he knew it, the better part of a year had gone by.

The young novice monk had been trying to come up with a mighty name for him, but a regular pilgrim beat him to it.
The pilgrim smiled and said that every time he climbed the mountain, the little yellow dog would always lead the way in silence, never barking, never yapping. A dog of few words, and a fine match for this quiet osmanthus courtyard.
"Let's call him Osmanthus, then!"

Late autumn came, and osmanthus blossoms drifted down through the trees onto Osmanthus's back. He shook out his coat, mildly put out by the sharp sweetness of the petals.
Heaven's fragrance in the osmanthus; clouds upon clouds of white.
Osmanthus let out an enormous sneeze, sprawled on the sun-warmed bluestone, and thought drowsily that he hadn't been in a fight in a long, long time.

禁中森严，人难越雷池，猫却总能莫名其妙地寻隙钻来。运道好的被贵人抱去，享泼天富贵；次些的被宫人喂养，也算有片瓦遮头。差的夹尾偷生，但也能受同类的帮携——毕竟猫虽有强弱，却不似人那般尊卑分明。人有主奴，但猫终究都是猫。

杂毛便是只初来乍到的猫，无名无姓，毛色玄黄驳杂。群猫环伺，杂毛矮矮蹲坐，紧紧用尾巴圈住两只前爪。良久，一只竖着尾巴的白猫踱步而出，上前碰了碰杂毛的鼻子。
杂毛知道，自己被默许留下了。

但宫里的规矩显然要多些。竖尾巴喵了一声，转头前去。杂毛懵懵懂懂跟上。一路上猫群的咪咪喵喵里，杂毛听懂了，它们要带它去见“大王显灵”。

猫群最后停在后苑一株花树下，齐齐蹲坐，仰望树梢。
杂毛跟着蹲下，呆呆望着。
这树真大。它想起宫墙外的树，也同它一般忍饥挨饿，生得枯瘦干瘪，不似这般枝繁叶茂。

云流过来，花瓣落下。悉悉索索。后苑的水波拍岸作响。
树上传来一声喵叫。
en:
The palace is strict, and men dare not cross the line, yet cats always find a way to slip through the gaps. The lucky ones are taken in by nobles to enjoy immense favor; the others are fed by servants, at least having a roof over their heads. The worst off live in the shadows, yet even they are helped by their kind, for though some cats are stronger than others, they do not share the human sense of hierarchy. Men have masters and slaves, but a cat is, after all, a cat.

Scruffy was a newcomer, nameless, with a coat of mottled black and yellow. Surrounded by the pack, Scruffy crouched low, tail wrapped tight around his front paws. After a long while, a white cat with a raised tail sauntered out and touched noses with Scruffy.
Scruffy knew he was allowed to stay.

But the palace had more rules. Straight-tail meowed and turned away. Scruffy followed blindly. Amidst the mews of the pack, Scruffy understood: they were taking him to see the "Ascension of the King."

The pack stopped beneath a flowering tree in the Rear Garden, sitting in a row, looking up at the branches.
Scruffy sat too, staring blankly.
The tree was massive. He remembered the trees outside the palace walls: starving like him, withered and dry, unlike this lush canopy.

Clouds drifted by, petals fell. Rustle. The water of the Rear Garden lapped against the shore.
A meow came from the tree.

zh:
丁笑常在夜深时磨剑。
无人知晓，这精于谋算之人，唯有此刻能放任心绪流淌。
每次磨剑，他都会想起儿时的往事。边塞那场惨败，父兄被定为无能战死，他亦受牵连下狱。当时他想，自己再不是那个握笔的小公子了，那么等他自由了，他应当有一把剑，一把能划破不公、刺穿委屈、比父兄软弱无力的刀还要勇猛严酷的好剑。
可这些年，他恨着、磨着，剑越磨越亮，心却越磨越茫，怎也看不见前路……
这剑，究竟该指向何处？
直到中渡桥风云渐起，他知道了某个遥远的真相。
或许，它是该出鞘了，指向那些——该被清算的往事。
en:
Ding Xiao often sharpened his sword late at night.
No one knew that this man, so skilled in calculation, could only let his emotions flow at this moment.
Every time he sharpened his blade, he thought of his childhood. The crushing defeat at the frontier, his father and brothers branded as incompetent in death, and his own imprisonment. He thought then that he was no longer the young noble with a pen; when he was free, he should have a sword, a sword that could slice through injustice, pierce through grievances, and be more valiant and stern than his father's weak knives.
But all these years, as he hated and sharpened, the sword grew brighter, but his heart grew more lost, unable to see the path ahead...
Where exactly should this sword be pointed?
Until the clouds began to stir at Zhongdu Bridge, and he learned a distant truth.
Perhaps it was time for it to be unsheathed, pointed at past events that must be settled.

zh:
叔父： 
距那夜佛堂叔父与我密谈，已十二载过去。

那时您说，禄伯，你既接此旗，我有三事托你。
我满口应承，心想世间事若我奋力而为，岂有做不到的？

三事其一，佑百姓温饱，其二，护边陲太平。
我与您相约，若得丰收，便以吉金铸六畜兴旺之礼送至长安。您说四畜即可，吉金还是多留些给百姓铸农具吧。 
至于第三事……等我完成了这两事再告诉我。

而今，边陲阡陌之间，百姓今年新种之苗已初现新绿，凉州亦再复归。承托的二事均已办妥，您未说的第三事……到底是什么？
en:
Uncle,
Twelve years have passed since our secret talk in the Buddhist shrine that night.
You said to me then, "Huaishen, since you have taken up this banner, there are three behests I must entrust to you." I agreed without hesitation, believing that if I fought with all my might, nothing in this world would be beyond my reach.

The first was to ensure the people are fed and clothed. The second, to safeguard the frontier's peace.
We agreed that upon a bountiful year, we would forge a bronze Harvest Tribute and send it to Chang'an. You said four beasts would suffice for the tribute, wishing to spare the remaining bronze for the people to forge farming tools.
As for the third behest... you told me to complete the first two before you would reveal it.

Now, fresh green shoots are sprouting across the borderlands, and Liangzhou has been fully restored. The first two behests you entrusted to me are done. What exactly is the third?

zh:
青啊青，你既有幸加入这墨门，和这么多优秀的人一起学习，一定要记得每日三省吾身——按时赴约否、按时赴约否、按时赴约否？
……
八月十七，一个不小心，让万师师兄在墨守亭吹了一下午的秋风。
真是有苦衷啊！在看拂菻人耍大刀时，竟遇见个闹事的……本只想吓唬吓唬那人，可真气沿着剑身打出去，竟把那人掀飞了好几米，到头来还得陪着人家上医馆。哎，此事若告师兄，必引其嗤笑。索性准备点赔罪礼，上次给他带的那本水利古籍原本被我放哪里了来着？哦对，回山路上与山匪打斗，不小心被我劈成两半，虽已拼合……唉，还是亲手誊抄一份，再去向师兄赔罪吧！
……
十月初二，今日与师论道，争执方酣，师父又颓然入梦。我岂能容他借眠遁理？于是守在书房等他醒来，这一等，竟星斗满天……误了和启蛰师兄的共膳之约，闭门反思数天，终于绣完这幅方帕。只是这上面飞鸟，愈看愈像一只落水的大肥鸭……启蛰师兄……应是不介意的……可我……还是勤练手艺吧。
……
正月廿三，要命了要命了！这次真的是运炁运迷糊了，都忘了和师父约好去钓大鱼！
不过师父自己也老是打瞌睡，说不定，他也没记住时间呢？不行不行，这不就是欺师吗？欸，对了！不如削一支竹簪给师父？别的手艺不好说，我使剑还是有两下子的。
正好让师父把他那头飘飘秀发挽起来，这样他打瞌睡的时候，就不会一直哈秋哈秋的，被自个儿头发痒醒啦！
……
en:
Halcyon, oh Halcyon. Now that you've had the good fortune to join Mohist Hill and study alongside so many remarkable people, you must remember to examine yourself three times a day: did you make it on time, did you make it on time, did you make it on time?
...
17th Day of the Eighth Month
One careless slip today left Senior Brother Wanshi waiting in the autumn wind at Confluence Gazebo for the whole afternoon.
I really did have my reasons. While watching a Roman man perform with a great blade, I ran into someone making trouble. I only meant to scare him a little, but my qi ran straight down the sword and sent him flying several meters. In the end, I even had to take him to the clinic. If I tell Senior Brother, he'll definitely laugh at me, so I may as well prepare an apology gift instead. Now then, where did I put that old waterworks text I brought him last time? Oh, right. I split it in half by accident while fighting bandits on the way back to the mountain. I did patch it back together, but... sigh. Better copy out a new one by hand and go apologize properly.
...
2nd Day of the Tenth Month
Today I was discussing the Dao with Master, and just as the argument was getting good, he nodded off again. How could I let him dodge reason with a nap? So I stayed in the study waiting for him to wake, and by the time he did, the stars were already out...
Which meant I missed my meal with Senior Brother Qizhe. I shut myself away for several days to reflect, and at last finished embroidering this square handkerchief. Only, the bird on it looks more like a big fat duck that fell in the water... Senior Brother Qizhe... probably won't mind... but I... had better keep practicing my needlework.
...
23rd Day of the First Month
This is bad. Truly bad. This time I really did get so muddled from circulating my qi that I completely forgot I'd promised Master we'd go catch a big fish.

The adults never let them have much. Too sweet, they say. Bad for the teeth.
So of course the children wait for a moment when no one is looking, snatch a piece, and shove it into their mouths.
Then an adult spots them and calls out, "Hey, not that one. That one's gone bad."
But the child just keeps chewing, cheeks puffed out, and somehow it still tastes sweet.
Maybe the room is too warm. Maybe the laughter is too loud. Maybe everyone looks too happy for anything to taste wrong.

zh:
冰魄魄终于给自己的第三个家家建好了门。满头的尘土，呛得她打了个喷嚏。
她也不知道为什么阿爷阿娘一定要求自己盖三个房子。家里的十几个兄弟姐妹都被爷娘要求盖三个房子。
明明有一个能容身睡觉的地方就足够。三个家，还要三把锁。从此，冰魄魄每天都要思考今天到底要去哪个家。
不说别的，单单是找出每一个家对应的钥匙，就快把冰魄魄逼疯了。
有一天，爷娘把兄弟姐妹们聚在一起。冰魄魄终于问出来自己的疑问。
爷娘相视一眼，轻轻叹了一口气。
“在很久很久以前，你们的爷爷的爷爷的爷爷还在世的时候。”
“那时候我们都还只有一个家。每天进进出出，也自由方便。”
故事进行到这里，就该进入“突然”的环节了。冰魄魄紧张地咽了咽口水。
“突然有一天，一群野匪顺着路，推开了家门。家里的一切都被掳走了。”
“那，然后呢？”一位兄弟害怕地出声询问。
“当然是全没了。房子，塌了，家财，没了。”
“所以，盖三个房子，是为了给我们留个生机啊！”爷娘适时地叮嘱。“只有让别人都猜不到你在哪个家，你才可能保住性命。”
众兄弟姐妹们点点头。但冰魄魄仍没解开心中的疑惑。
“好烂的故事……盖了三个房子，目标更多，不是损失更大么？”
en:
Ice Soul finally finished building the door for her third house. Covered in dust, she sneezed. 
She didn't understand why her parents insisted she build three houses. All her dozen or so siblings were ordered to build three houses each. 
Wasn't one place to sleep and take shelter enough? Three houses also meant three locks. From then on, Ice Soul had to decide every day which house she would stay in. 
Just finding the right key for each house was driving her mad. 
One day, her parents gathered all the siblings together. Ice Soul finally voiced her question. 
Her parents looked at each other and sighed softly. 
"A very, very long time ago, when your great-great-grandfather was still alive..." 
"Back then, we all had just one home. Coming and going was free and easy." 
At this point in the story, it was time for the "suddenly" part. Ice Soul swallowed nervously. 
"Suddenly, one day, a group of bandits followed the road and pushed open the door. Everything in the house was stolen." 
"Then... what happened?" one brother asked fearfully. 
"Everything was gone, of course. The house collapsed, the family wealth was lost." 
"So, building three houses is to give us a chance at survival!" her parents took the opportunity to advise. "Only by keeping everyone guessing which house you're in can you possibly save your life." 
All the siblings nodded. But Ice Soul still hadn't resolved her confusion. 
"What a lame story... Building three houses just gives them more targets, wouldn't the losses be even bigger?"

未寄出的信二：
先生所荐斑蝥，确有些效验，但终究治标不治本。不过余已另寻得一条明路——江南苏家有一味能平百气、解百毒的神药。余拟登门求取，先生不必再挂心了。
en:
Letter One:
To the esteemed Master Xu: In your letter, you describe that after each "taking of medicine," your vital energy surges violently, and your flesh swells and warps beneath the skin—a most ominous sign of stagnant, turbid blood accumulated to its extreme. Yet as you conceal your illness and shun proper treatment, refusing to name plainly what manner of potent, perilous tonic you have consumed, I have no means of prescribing a true remedy. For now, I have added to the original formula a measure of "blister beetle"—a creature fierce in nature and highly toxic, yet possessed of tremendous power to break stagnant blood and dispel congestion. Should even this fierce medicine fail to suppress the affliction, then I fear there is nothing more I can do.

Unsent Letter Two:
The blister beetle you recommended, Master, has indeed shown some effect, but in the end it treats the symptom, not the root. However, I have since found another path—the Su family of Jiangnan possesses a wondrous remedy said to calm all kinds of vital energies and dissolve all kinds of poisons. I intend to call upon them in person to seek it out; you need trouble yourself no further on my account.
Nalan Manqiu

zh:
缺角的小日记

娘说，她不是不要我们。
她是在和我们玩捉迷藏。
她说，等病好了，就来找我们。
找到以后，带我们去后山踢球。

我们把球放在门口。
这样娘来找我们的时候，就知道我们还在。

可是天黑了好久。

她还没来。
en:
Torn Diary

Mother said she isn't leaving us. She's playing hide-and-seek.
She said when she gets better, she'll come find us. When she does, she'll take us to kick a ball up the back mountain.
We left the ball by the door. So when Mother comes looking, she'll know we're still here.

But it's been dark for a long time now.

She hasn't come.

zh:
篝火旁有八人围坐。就在几日前，这八个人还只是一群素未谋面的陌生人。但为了在契丹的铁骑下护住这片土地和这里的百姓，他们自愿留下来商议执行对策。连日来，他们改建地道、安置百姓，几乎没有合眼。如今万事具备，他们才得空坐在篝火前聊起各自的身份与来历。绳文绳武是一对双胞胎，哥哥绳文是个儒雅的青年，而弟弟绳武看着也如他的名字一般孔武有力，不过听绳文说他这弟弟并不会说话。一群人喝了点酒便打开了话匣子，绳文说起两兄弟从前，不过是皮影戏匠，可因为弟弟不会说话，最后还是被赶了出来。

绳文说到激动处便猛灌了两口酒，愤愤地说：“真不甘心，此番去燕南定要闯出一番名堂，也好让那些欺辱过我们的人瞧瞧！”
绳武瞧见哥哥的模样也跟着灌了两口。
“那万一闯不出名堂，还一不小心死了呢？”人群里一位白发须眉的老人笑问道。
绳文此时已然醉了，意识模糊间他心想就是死了又如何？
“那就往东走，往西走，再走远一些，走到哪儿算哪儿……”话还没说完，绳文已沉沉睡去。
en:
Around the campfire sat eight people. Just days ago, they had been strangers. But to protect this land and its people from the Khitan's iron cavalry, they had chosen to stay, planning, preparing, fighting. For days, they had rebuilt tunnels, evacuated civilians, and were barely sleeping. Now, with everything in place, they finally had a moment to rest by the fire and share their stories. Among them were twin brothers—Sheng Wen, a refined scholar, and Sheng Wu, who lived up to his name with a warrior's build. But Sheng Wen explained that his brother was mute. After a few drinks, the group grew talkative, and Sheng Wen began recounting how the two had once been shadow play artisans, only to be driven out because his brother could not speak.

Drunk on anger and liquor, Sheng Wen took another swig. "I refuse to accept this fate. When we reach Yannan, we'll make our names known. Let those who scorned us choke on their regret!"
Sheng Wu mimicked his brother and took a few gulps too.
"And what if you don't make it and end up dead by accident?" asked an old man with white hair and whiskers, smiling.
Sheng Wen, now thoroughly drunk, barely registered the question. What did it matter?
"Then we'll walk east, walk west, go even farther... just keep going until we can't go anymore..." Before he finished, Sheng Wen had fallen into a deep sleep.

zh:
【缁衣第三十三】

子言之曰：“为上易事也，为下易知也，则刑不烦矣。”子曰：“好贤如《缁衣》，恶恶如《巷伯》，则爵不渎而民作愿，刑不试而民咸服。大雅曰：‘仪刑文王，万国作孚。’”子曰：“夫民，教之以德，齐之以礼，则民有格心；教之以政，齐之以刑，则民有遁心。故君民者，子以爱之，则民亲之；信以结之，则民不倍；恭以莅之，则民有孙心。《甫刑》曰：‘苗民罪用命，制以刑，惟作五虐之刑曰法。是以民有恶德，而遂绝其世也。’”
子曰：“下之事上也，不从其所令，从其所行。上好是物，下必有甚者矣。故上之所好恶，不可不慎也，是民之表也。”子曰：“禹立三年，百姓以仁遂焉，岂必尽仁？《诗》云：‘赫赫师尹，民具尔瞻。’《甫刑》曰：‘一人有庆，兆民赖之。’大雅曰：‘成王之孚，下土之式。’”子曰：“上好仁，则下之为仁争先人。故长民者章志、贞教、尊仁，以子爱百姓；民致行己以说其上矣。《诗》云：‘有梏德行，四国顺之。’”
子曰：“王言如丝，其出如纶；王言如纶，其出如綍。故大人不倡游言。可言也，不可行。君子弗言也；可行也，不可言，君子弗行也。则民言不危行，而行不危言矣。《诗》云：‘淑慎尔止，不愆于仪。’”子曰：“君子道人以言，而禁人以行。故言必虑其所终，而行必稽其所敝；则民谨于言而慎于行。《诗》云：‘慎尔出话，敬尔威仪。’大雅曰：‘穆穆文王，于缉熙敬止。’”
子曰：“长民者，衣服不贰，从容有常，以齐其民，则民德壹。《诗》云：‘彼都人士，狐裘黄黄，其容不改，出言有章，行归于周，万民所望。’”子曰：“为上可望而知也，为下可述而志也，则君不疑于其臣，而臣不惑于其君矣。《尹吉》曰：‘惟尹躬及汤，咸有壹德。’《诗》云：‘淑人君子，其仪不忒。’”
子曰：“有国者章义瘅恶，以示民厚，则民情不贰。《诗》云：‘靖共尔位，好是正直。’”子曰：“上人疑则百姓惑，下难知则君长劳。故君民者，章好以示民俗，慎恶以御民之淫，则民不惑矣。臣仪行，不重辞，不援其所不及，不烦其所不知，则君不劳矣。《诗》云：‘上帝板板，下民卒瘅。’小雅曰：‘匪其止共，惟王之邛。’”
……
en:
【Black Robes, Chapter Thirty-Three】

The Master said: "When the ruler is easy to serve and the subjects are easy to understand, then punishments will not be troublesome." The Master said: "If one loves the worthy as in 'Black Robes' and hates the wicked as in 'Xiang Bo,' then titles will not be debased and the people will aspire to goodness; punishments need not be applied and the people will all submit. The Greater Odes say: 'Pattern yourself after King Wen, and the myriad states will trust you.'" The Master said: "For the people, if you teach them with virtue and regulate them with propriety, they will have hearts that turn to good; if you teach them with governance and regulate them with punishments, they will have hearts that seek to evade. Therefore, one who rules the people should love them as sons, and the people will draw near; bind them with trust, and the people will not betray; approach them with reverence, and the people will have hearts of deference. The 'Punishments of Fu' say: 'The Miao people refused to use good commands, so they were controlled with punishments, creating five cruel punishments and calling it law. Thus the people had evil virtues, and their line was cut off.'"
The Master said: "When subordinates serve their superiors, they do not follow their commands but follow their actions. If the superior likes a thing, those below will surely exceed him in it. Therefore, what the superior likes and dislikes must not be taken lightly, for he is the model for the people." The Master said: "When Yu stood for three years, the people achieved benevolence through him—how could they all have been inherently benevolent? The Odes say: 'Majestic is Master Yin; the people all look to you.' The 'Punishments of Fu' say: 'When one man has blessings, the myriad people rely on them.' The Greater Odes say: 'The trust of King Cheng is the pattern for all under heaven.'" The Master said: "If the superior loves benevolence, then those below will strive to be first in benevolence. Therefore, one who leads the people should make his will clear, teach with integrity, honor benevolence, and love the people as sons; then the people will exert themselves to please him. The Odes say: 'With virtuous conduct as a restraint, the four quarters follow him.'"
The Master said: "When the king's words are like silk, their issuance is like cord; when the king's words are like cord, their issuance is like rope. Therefore, great men do not advocate idle speech. What can be spoken but not practiced—the gentleman does not speak it; what can be practiced but not spoken—the gentleman does not do it. Then the people's words will not endanger their deeds, nor their deeds endanger their words. The Odes say: 'Be careful and proper in your demeanor, and do not err in your bearing.'" The Master said: "The gentleman guides people with words and restrains them with deeds. Therefore, in speech one must consider its end, and in deeds one must examine its flaws; then the people will be careful in speech and cautious in deeds. The Odes say: 'Be careful in your speech, and reverent in your dignity.' The Greater Odes say: 'Solemn is King Wen, radiant in reverent stillness.'"
The Master said: "One who leads the people should not vary his attire, and should be composed and constant, to unify his people; then the people's virtue will be single. The Odes say: 'Those gentlemen of the capital, with yellow fox-fur robes, their demeanor unchanging, their speech patterned, returning to Zhou, the hope of all the people.'" The Master said: "When the superior can be known at a glance, and the subordinate can be described and remembered, then the ruler will not doubt his ministers, and the ministers will not be confused about their ruler. The 'Yin Ji' say: 'I, Yin, and Tang both possessed single virtue.' The Odes say: 'The good man and gentleman, his bearing is without error.'"
The Master said: "One who holds a state should make righteousness clear and condemn evil, to show the people generosity; then the people's hearts will not be divided. The Odes say: 'Be still in your position, and love what is upright.'" The Master said: "If the superior is doubtful, the people will be confused; if those below are hard to understand, the ruler will labor. Therefore, one who rules the people should make clear what is good to show the people's customs, and be cautious in what he hates to guard against the people's excesses; then the people will not be confused. If ministers model their conduct, do not stress words, do not reach for what cannot be attained, and do not trouble others with what they do not know, then the ruler will not labor. The Odes say: 'God is contrary, and the people below are utterly distressed.' Xiao Ya says: 'Not in their service, but in the king's toil.'"

zh:
绳文、绳武兄弟自幼流落江湖，以皮影为生。绳文擅唱腔，故专唱和之事。绳武擅武术，故为兄掌中肉影。兄弟二人一唱一武，渐于皮影之中领悟一套大开大合的武学。后来山河破碎，兄弟二人应征抗敌。与其中佼佼者合为河东八俊，护佑清河渡过此国祸之难。河山终固，但那些随兄弟二人一同奋战的人，却早已逝去，无人记忆。唯有兄弟二人时常于北盟之畔，演练皮影，那是他们曾经的苦难，亦是他们记得那些魂灵的记忆。
入戏者，当有入戏之苦。若碰上了兄弟二人，且记终了此幕，将兄弟二人唤醒。
en:
Brothers Sheng Wen and Sheng Wu were cast in the Jianghu since childhood, making a living by puppetry. Shengwen excels in singing, specializing in harmonic melodies, while Shengwu masters martial arts, manipulating the shadow figures for his brother. Through their combined singing and martial movements, the brothers gradually developed a broad-sweeping martial art from shadow puppetry. When the country fell into chaos, they enlisted to resist the enemy, joining forces with elite warriors to form the "Eight Talents of Hedong," protecting Qinghe through the national crisis. Though the land was finally stabilized, those who fought alongside them have long passed, forgotten by most. Now, the brothers often perform shadow puppetry by the shores of Northern Vow, a ritual that honors both their past sufferings and the spirits of the fallen. 
Those who lose themselves in the play must bear its suffering. If you encounter the two brothers, be sure to end this act and awaken them from their trance.

en: Atop the ridge stands a stone tower of imposing grandeur, bare of vermilion lacquer. From its roof hangs a great bell. When the wind passes, it rings out, its sound deep and rolling as thunder. The cliff face is steep in its sheer drop; beams of wood are laid across it as a path, spiraling upward tier upon tier, like a suspended ladder pressed against the wall. Those who ascend make their way along the wood. On one side, a perilous overhang of rock bears down from above; on the other, a sea of clouds churns and surges, stirring heart and soul alike. Where the bell's sound rises, all the mountains answer in echo, and all other sounds fall into silence. When that golden voice rings out once, all the world knows where learning is bound.

zh:
他的窝窝头总被别人抢去半个，他也不说话，只是握着剩下半个窝窝头，跑到更远的角落，将仅剩的东西往嘴里塞去，吃快点，就不会被抢了。
他听见别人的笑话声，说他样样不行，逃跑最快，他也不敢争辩，既然，半个窝窝头也能活，能活就好了，为什么要动手呢。
所以他们说他是怂包软蛋。

这样的怂包软蛋本是不应该来当兵的。
他的剑第一次插入对面人的胸膛，看着一双怨恨的眼睛，眼泪流的比血更多，他手抖得厉害，割下那个人的耳朵，那个耳朵的边缘锯得实在不平。
等下了战场，回到军营。
“床上那个不会是死了吧，欸！咋半天没动静。”
“见血了，怕呗，要是得了军功，我就回家，才不在这儿。”
“这军中可不是谁都和咱们一样，那王清将军有个义子，那才是金贵人，用不着刀口舔血。”
“听说原本也就是个没人要的，现在命好，真是脸面，成日喝酒惹事，混得很，没人管。”
“喂，那个死的——靠！怎么忽然没声响地坐起来，你叫啥？——问你呢！几岁啊！叫啥名！”
“十三、十三，贺、贺然。”

“啧！你爹娘读过书？”
“没爹娘。”
“那这世道还有人这么好心，给你起个像人的名字。”
他坐在那儿不说话，舔了舔嘴唇，“有的、有的，将军起的。”
他听见那些人嗤笑的声音。“将军？哟！杀了个人还吓出个瘟梦了，你说的是哪个泥头地里的蛐蛐将——淦！敢打老子？”
“将军就是将军。”
嗤笑的人抬头，看见一双发狠的眼睛，忽然发了怵：“疯子！老子不和你这疯子计较。”
en:
His cornbread was always robbed, half of it, every time. He never said a word. Just held the half that was left, ran to a distant corner, and stuffed it into his mouth. Eat faster, and there would be nothing left to steal.

He heard them laugh behind his back, saying he was useless, good at nothing except running away. He didn't dare talk back. After all, even half a cornbread could keep you alive. And if you could live, what was the point of fighting?

So they called him a coward. A soft-bellied coward.

Someone like that shouldn't have ended up in the army.

The first time his sword sank into a man's chest, he saw those eyes full of hatred. The tears came faster than the blood. His hands were shaking so badly as he sawed off the man's ear. The cut was jagged, uneven.

When he got back to camp,

"Hey, the one on that bed, is he dead or what? Hasn't moved in ages."

"First time seeing blood. Bet he's scared shitless. If I ever get a medal, I'm heading home. No way I'm staying here."

"Not everyone here's like us. That General Wang Qing's adopted son, that one's born lucky. Doesn't have to live on a knife's edge."

"Used to be a nobody too, I heard. Now he's all swagger and wine, causing trouble day in, day out. Nobody dares stop him."

"Hey! You dead or what? Holy shit! He just sat up without a sound. What's your name? Hey, You deaf? I said, what's your name? How old are you?"

"...Thirteen. He—He Ran."

"Tch. Such a fancy name. Your parents must be scholars or something!"

"I have no parents."

"Well damn. Someone still gave you a proper name? That's rare."

He didn't answer. Just licked his lips and muttered,

"Yeah... someone did. The General."

He heard them snort.

"The general? What, you dreaming now? Which muddy patch of dirt did you see that cricket of a general in—Hey?! You dare hit me?"

"...A general is a general."

The sneering soldier looked up and saw a pair of eyes, crazed and intent. For a moment, he flinched.

"...Psycho. I'm not messing with a lunatic."

从什么时候开始的呢……阿然想起来，对了，是那天晚上，有人唱歌的晚上。
有人在唱歌，所以她醒过来，坐在窗边听。
有人在怒吼，所以她朝着声音来的方向探出身，更专注地听。
起风了，叶子刷刷响，才叫回阿然的心神。
然后……然后呢？然后大侠就来啦，街上的叫卖多了，木头的朽味道少了。爹爹回来了！
对了，阿然还没有跟爹爹说过，大侠把金叶子带回来的那天晚上，她做了一个梦呢，梦见——
#Y【大火炉】——有个大侠从火炉上飞起来，飞得比月亮还高，喊着，苍生无言，侠为其声！这声音，比阿然听过的任何话都好听。#E
en:
Zheng Ran noticed that the crackling of fires in Kaifeng City had vanished, and the scorching, acrid smells had faded. When people walked down the streets, the jingle of the coin pouches in their robes sounded somehow fuller and weightier.
When did it begin...? Right, it was that night, the night someone was singing.
That singing woke her, so she sat by the window to listen.
Someone was roaring in anger, so she leaned out toward the sound, listening even more intently.
The wind picked up, and the rustling leaves brought Ran back to her senses.
Then... what happened then? Then the wanderer arrived! The street vendors' cries grew livelier, and the stench of rotting wood faded. Father came home!
Oh, right! Ran still hasn't told Father that on the night the wanderer brought back the gold leaf, she had a dream. She dreamed of...
#Y[The Great Furnace] A wanderer leapt from the blazing furnace and soared higher than the moon, crying out, "People's Voice!" To Ran, this voice was more beautiful than anything she had ever heard.#E

zh:
一直以来，黎蓁蓁的世界都是一片漆黑。
因为看不见事物，便被剥夺了成为人的自由。
推搡、咒骂、厌弃、恶意，然后一小袋铜钱，买断她一生的归属。
她从未想过反抗，因为她从未听说过反抗。她以为所有人都如她一般，如无根的浮萍，随波顺水，在没有出路的宿命之海中打转，最终慢慢淹死。
所以，被卖给那家人做奴做仆之时，她什么都没说。要嫁给那个快病死的疯子之时，她什么都没说。新婚之夜发疯的众人举刀逼近她之时，她也什么都没说，只是垂下了头，像羊一样露出细瘦脆弱的脖颈。

直到那些刀被另一把刀弹开。
那个少年将小小的短剑塞进她的手中，她才明白原来世上竟有另一种选择。
那些曾经欺辱她的人，在见到她的剑后，竟也会跪地求饶，像她曾经那样颤抖。

有人问后来的月神，为什么选择成为一名剑客。她没有说话，只是轻轻摸了摸自己的剑。
剑，便是她在这人世通行的唯一依靠。
en:
For as long as Li Zhenzhen can remember, her world is shrouded in darkness.
Blind since birth, she is robbed of the simple freedom to live as others do.
Shoved, cursed, detested, her life is defined by the cruel treatment of others. All of it can be summed up by a small bag of copper coins, the price of her fate.
Rebellion is a thought she never entertains. She has never even heard of rebellion. To her, it seems everyone lives the same way, like rootless reeds drifting aimlessly on a vast, indifferent river, carried by the currents of fate, destined to sink into its depths.
So, when she was sold to that family as a servant and slave, she said nothing. When they promised her to a sick, deranged man, she said nothing. On their wedding night, when the crowd closed in, knives in hand, she remained silent. She simply lowered her head, exposing her fragile neck, like a sheep waiting for slaughter.

Then, in that moment of helplessness, another blade intercepted the knives.
A young man pressed a short sword into her hand, and in that instant, she realized there was another way.
The people who once tormented her now kneel before her, trembling at the sight of the blade in her hand, just as she had once trembled before theirs.

Later, someone asks the Lunar Goddess why she chooses the path of a swordswoman. She never answers. Instead, she gently touches her sword. 
It is the only tool she has ever needed to survive in this world.

zh:
公主府的人说，公主是天下权势最大的女人。
皇帝的废立都在公主的一念之间，更何况一个小小的江湖门派？
得了公主命令的他们，毫不犹豫砸了道真的祠堂，只为拿走供奉在那里的无量剑。
至于那祠堂怎么样了，公主不在乎，他们不在乎，雩真当然也不应当在乎。

他们因此沉溺在煊赫的声势当中，张扬、猖狂又大意。
也是，如果这天下都要落在他们主子手中，甚至在他们看来，已经落到手中——
谁能让这群凡夫保持警醒，保持高尚，保持夙兴夜寐的勤勉和谦卑？
谁都不能。即使他们尝到恶果，也不能。
en:
The people of the Princess's manor liked to say that their mistress was the most powerful woman under heaven. If even the rise and fall of emperors rested on a single thought of hers, what was one small jianghu sect to them?
With the Princess's order in hand, they smashed Daozhen's shrine without hesitation, all to take the Wuliang Blade enshrined there. As for what became of the shrine, the Princess did not care, and neither did they. In their eyes, Yuzhen should not have cared either.
So they sank deeper into the splendor of borrowed power, loud, arrogant, and careless. And why not? If the realm itself was soon to fall into their master's hands, or so they believed, then who could possibly make such people stay vigilant, decent, diligent, or humble?
No one. Not even after they tasted the consequences.
Stench · Level III

zh: 酥锅最早大概起源于制瓷窑工将各种菜混放在砂锅中炖煮的大锅菜，据传后经一位苏姓女子改良，方有了苏锅。又因此膳用醋较多，鱼酥肉烂，便改名酥锅，其中的菜肴被称为酥菜。民间为了增添此菜的传奇色彩，将酥锅的发明与北宋著名美食家苏东坡的妹妹苏小妹联系了起来。不过苏小妹史载并无此人，乃是后人杜撰，但这并不妨碍她作为古代女子智慧的化身所展现出的耀眼光芒。
en: Assorted Stew, also known as "Su Guo," likely originates among porcelain kiln workers, who stew a mix of ingredients together in large pots. It is later refined by a woman surnamed Su, but the dish's name comes not only from her, but also from its long simmering time and heavy use of vinegar, which leaves the fish tender and the meat meltingly soft. Folklore further embellishes its origin, crediting its invention to Su Xiaomei, the fictional sister of the famed Song Dynasty gourmet Su Dongpo. Though not a historical figure, Su Xiaomei lives on as a symbol of culinary wit and feminine ingenuity.

zh:
世上的人改头换面，抛下过去，有的是为了未来，有的是为了当下，有的是为了钱，有的是为了情，有的是为了骗自己。
但在这身黑甲穿上的瞬间，他意识到，抛下过去不是能给自己换来什么，只有抛下。
抛下过去，也抛下未来，抛下名字，也抛下荣誉，抛下和那世间所有联系。
他听见有人念了一句。
“穿上了，就脱不下来了。”
“我倒是不要紧，可……是最可惜的了。”

是别人说的吗，还是他自己？他已经记不清了。

他记不清他是否在那个瞬间抬起头，向着天、不、这里已经看不见天了。
当一个人生活在地面之时，他抬头所望，看见的是天，当一个人生活在地底之时，他抬头所仰望，所能看到的便是地面上的世间。
但二者，对于下一刻的他而言，将没有什么区别，都是无法到达的地方。
他总归记不得了，他是不是最后望了一眼世间。

当日子相似到每一日都是前一日的轮回之时，时间如同重复的水流，将记忆的石板磨损得体无完肤，他只是坐在这里擦拭着手中的兵器，这时候他总会看见自己掌心的旧茧，数道旧伤，他偶尔停下，看上几眼。
像是在看另一个人的一生。
en:
In this world, people change their names, their faces, and cast off the past—some for the future, some for the present, some for money, some for love, and some just to deceive themselves. But the moment he put on that black armor, he understood that leaving the past behind wouldn't earn him anything. To cast it off was simply to cast it off.

Cast off the past, the future, his name, his honor, and every thread tying him to the world.

He heard someone whisper:

"Once you put it on, you can't take it off."

"It's not a problem for me, but... it's such a shame."

Was it someone else who said it? Or had he said it himself? He couldn't remember.

He couldn't remember if, in that moment, he had looked up. Looked up toward the sky. No—there was no sky here anymore.

When a man lives on the surface, he looks up and sees the heavens. But when a man lives underground, when he looks up, all he sees is the world above.

And for him, in the next moment, there would be no difference between the two. Both were places he could no longer reach.

He couldn't remember whether he had looked back one last time at the world.

When each day becomes a perfect echo of the last, time flows like water, wearing down his memory to a smooth, blank stone. He would simply sit and polish his weapon. And sometimes, his gaze would fall to the old calluses in his palm, the faded scars across his hand. Sometimes, he would pause and stare at them for a moment or two. As though he were watching someone else's entire life.

重修登云梯记

此间山脉，高崖峻壁，鸟道难寻。墨门居绥乡，而飞天城据天陉之巅，旧有登云梯，循石磴而上，宛若凌霄，乃古人凿岩架木，以通往来。穷奇之祸后，石阶倾圮，危若悬釜，往来者多绕道数十里，艰于跋涉。
斯梯为南北之要冲，废则民不便，乃集众议，捐俸若干，募工匠精于石作者，取太行坚岩，斧削为磴，层层相接，间以铁链为扶，复置木梁于险处，使履者安。其役凡一月，日以晨昏，锤声振谷，石屑飞空，风雨不作，工遂速成。
梯成，凡高七十丈，曲折如虬，直上云表。行者自深泽登之，不半日可达天陉；自天陉下之，不伤足而至绥乡。弟子百姓由是往来，省道三十里；香客朝山，亦免崎岖。至晴明之日，凭梯北望，太行层峦如画，云影相接，真一奇观也。兼以附今岁月云。
en:
Record of Rebuilding the Cloudstair

These mountains feature towering cliffs, making paths hard to find. 
The Mohists reside in Suixiang, while Skyward City sits atop the Heaven's Threshold. The old Cloudstair ascended via stone steps into the clouds, built by ancients who carved rocks and laid timber for passage.
After the Qiongqi disaster, the stone steps collapsed, becoming dangerously steep. Travelers had to detour for miles, enduring arduous treks.
As a vital north-south route, its ruin inconvenienced the people. Funds were gathered to hire skilled stonemasons. They carved firm rocks from Mount Taihang into steps, linked them with iron chains, and placed wooden beams in perilous spots to ensure safe passage. The work took a month. From dawn to dusk, hammer blows echoed in the valley, and stone dust filled the air. Spared by wind and rain, the construction was swiftly completed.
Once completed, the ladder stood seventy rods high, winding like a dragon straight into the clouds.
Travelers climbing from Shenze can reach Heaven's Threshold in half a day. Descending from Heaven's Threshold to Suixiang is effortless. Disciples and commoners save thirty miles of travel, and pilgrims avoid rugged paths.
On clear days, looking north from the ladder, the picturesque Mount Taihang blends with the clouds—a true spectacle. Recorded on this date.

看炊烟怎么爬上傍晚，看霜花如何结满窗棂。

en:
It has been so long, our dear friend.

By the time you find this Moon Lantern, we will already be watching you from hiding.
You look so very much like the one who used to play hide and seek with us long ago.

We wanted Star Candy, and pain salve, and moonlight too.
But in the end, we decided to leave them all to you.
With this one moon, you will have everything.

Stand where the moon is nearest, and home will come into clearer view.
See how the cooking smoke climbs into the evening sky.
See how frost flowers gather upon the window lattice.
And look as well upon the road that brought you here, to see whether the moonlight will set it aglow.

Winter has come again.
Will you look forward to it, as we do?
Whether or not you are that person, please accept this piece of moonlight.

zh: 田弘正碑，韩愈撰文，立于家庙。田弘正原为魏博军衙内兵马使，后被士卒拥立为主，率六州之地归顺朝廷。元稹评价：“田宏正首以六州之众，归於朝廷，开先帝之雄图，变河朔之旧俗，除去苛暴，昭宣惠和，爱人如身，养士如子，拊循教训，必以忠孝为先，是以魏之师徒，一年而知恩，二年而知礼，三年而知相与让於道矣。故南征淮、蔡，东伐青、齐，北定赵地，元勋茂绩，皆自魏师。”
en: Composed by Han Yu and erected in the family temple. Tian Hongzheng was originally a military officer under the Weibo Army but was later proclaimed leader by his soldiers, surrendering six provinces to the imperial court. Yuan Zhen praised him: "Tian Hongzheng was the first to lead the six provinces back to the court, realizing the late emperor's grand strategy and transforming the old customs of Hebei. He abolished harsh laws, promoted kindness, loved his people as his own body, and nurtured his soldiers like his sons. He taught them loyalty and filial piety, so that within one year, the soldiers of Wei knew gratitude; within two, they understood propriety; and by the third, they yielded to one another on the roads. Thus, they campaigned south against Huai and Cai, east against Qing and Qi, and north to pacify Zhao. All these great achievements were born from the Wei army."

……
自六月始，国主遣客省使翟如璧入贡于汴，献金银、罗绮、茶药诸物。宋主受之，释唐降卒千人，悉遣归。此辈皆旧岁被俘者，裹创扶杖，渡江而还，乡人迎于江岸，多有泣下者。

市井传言，宋主此举意在怀柔。然降卒归营后，多补入神卫军空额，营中夜闻操练声，较前稍密。有老兵私语：“汴梁放我辈归，非慈心，乃养唐人自耗耳。”

en:
Jiangning Prefecture Secret Report Summary
...
Starting in June, the Emperor sent Province Commissioner Zhai Rubi to deliver a tribute of gold, silver, silk, tea, and medicine to Bianliang. The Lord of Song accepted the offerings and let a thousand captured Tang soldiers go home. These men were all taken prisoner last year. Bandaged up and leaning on canes, they crossed the river to get back. Locals welcomed them at the bank, many shedding tears.

Word on the street is that the Song Emperor did this to win us over. But after those soldiers got back to camp, most of them were drafted to fill Imperial Vanguard vacancies. Nightly drill sounds in the camp are more frequent now. A veteran whispered privately, "Kaifeng did not release us out of mercy, but rather to let the Tang people exhaust themselves."

Your disciple has personally verified these truths and recorded them for your eyes. Any further developments will be reported immediately.
