zh:
我在海边采风，走着走着肚子就饿了，正巧碰上几个灶户，他们让我来这儿，说到了就有饭吃，还不收银子……
果真如此！甫一进村，热情的小伙子就迎了上来，拉着我往大院走。他也不问我姓甚名谁，打哪来的，便催着我落座，又念了好长一串菜名，我还没听清呢，就瞧见！院子里有好大一圈炉灶！
乡亲们围在一起，烟气、油响、香味搅在一块儿，炒菜的、翻勺的、淋汁的，好不热闹！我虽不会做饭，看着也手痒了，恨不得抢把铲子上去翻两下。
糖醋鲤鱼、四喜丸子、葱烧海参、芙蓉鸡片、红烧大肠……菜一道接一道地上，愣是没见着重样！天咧，这么多好吃的，我眼都花了，不知该从哪里下筷子。
这村子哪哪都好，乡亲们热络大方，和和气气，可我总觉得有点怪，这儿的文津馆弟子，跟别处见到的貌似不大一样……哦！我知道了，他们都没戴头纱！这是啥讲究呢？
不行，等我吃饱了，非得拽人问个明白。
en:
I was strolling along the coast, gathering inspiration, when my stomach suddenly started rumbling. As luck would have it, I bumped into a few coastal cooks who told me to come here. They promised there would be food waiting, and they wouldn't even charge me a single copper...
And they were right! The moment I stepped into the village, a warm, energetic young lad rushed up to greet me and dragged me toward a massive courtyard. Without asking for my name or where I came from, he urged me to take a seat and began rattling off a long list of dishes. Before I could even catch the names, I saw it: a massive ring of roaring stoves right in the middle of the courtyard!
The villagers were gathered tightly around. The smoke, the sizzling of oil, and the mouth-watering aromas all mixed together. People were stir-frying, tossing heavy woks, and drizzling rich sauces. It was a spectacular scene of bustling life! Even though I don't know the first thing about cooking, my hands were itching to grab a spatula and give it a toss myself.
Sweet and Sour Carp, Four-Joy Meatballs, Leek-Braised Sea Cucumber, Hibiscus Chicken, Braised Chitterlings... Plate after plate arrived at the table, and not a single dish was repeated! Heavens above, there was so much glorious food that my eyes were dazzled, and I didn't even know where to point my chopsticks first.
Everything about this village is wonderful. The locals are warm, generous, and incredibly friendly. Yet, I can't shake the feeling that something is a bit strange. The disciples of the Inkbound Order here look somehow different from the ones I've seen elsewhere... Oh! I've got it! None of them are wearing veils! What kind of tradition is that?
No, I can't let this go. Once I'm full, I absolutely must grab someone and ask for the story behind it.

香花雾：遮挡敌人的视野，持续3秒
乱花絮：颠倒敌人的移动操作，持续5秒
急东风：全队移动速度提升，持续5秒
催花雨：附近立刻开出本队伍的花
6、参与对局完成挑战任务，领取#Y配饰【陶乐乐】#E！
en:
1. Participate solo or team up with a friend.
2. A match includes 4 teams. Within 2 minutes, the team that generates the most flowers earns the highest points.
3. Teams can choose the faction [Carefree Oriole] or [Twin Swallows]. One match has 2 [Carefree Oriole] and 2 [Twin Swallows] teams. By default, [Carefree Oriole] possesses Fleethoof, while [Twin Swallows] can allow two players to cooperate, but they are restricted by a Red String.
4. After the match starts, moving causes your team's flowers to grow behind you. Flowers from different teams can cover each other. Meanwhile, items randomly refresh on the field; picking them up provides powerful assistance.
5. Items include:
Fragrant Mist: Obscures enemies' vision for 3 seconds
Chaotic Fluff: Inverts enemies' movement controls for 5 seconds
Swift East Wind: Increases movement speed for the entire team for 5 seconds
Flower-hastening Rain: Immediately causes your team's flowers to bloom nearby
6. Participate in the match and complete Challenge Quests to claim the accessory #Y"Clay Delight"#E!

When the Great Tang ascended, it was a dragon taking flight. Mount Hua was its mighty horn, the Yellow River its shimmering scales. The dragon has two eyes: one in Chang'an, and one in Hearthfall. Now that Chang'an has been lost, the dragon is half-blind, and the destiny of the empire falters.
Our sect has deciphered the celestial mandate and secured the Golden Peach. We now commence the rite of "Dragon's Awakening" in Hearthfall Hamlet. We shall elect a new lord to restore balance to heaven and earth.

All disciples must execute their sworn duties without fail.

千年以降，栾城其名与隶属历经更迭，后梁时曾因讳而改为栾氏县，今复称栾城县。
栾城民风淳朴，本以耕种为生，然近岁战火连天，黎民涂炭，生路几近断绝。幸蒙封龙书院相助，织造土布，闻名一方，解生计之忧；又得墨门机关术相授，机关精巧，御敌有序，待不时之需。
en:
On the banks of the Hutuo River stands a small town, surrounded by striking mountains and waterways, a place of natural advantage. In the Spring and Autumn period, the Jin minister Luan Shu held this land as his fief, and from him it took the name Luancheng.
Over the centuries, Luancheng's name and administrative affiliation changed more than once. During the Later Liang, it was renamed Luanshi County to observe a naming taboo, but today it is once again called Luancheng County.
The people of Luancheng were long simple farming folk, but years of war have brought them to the brink. Thankfully, with help from Dragonbend Academy, their homespun cloth has become known throughout the region, easing their hardship. They have also learned Mohist mechanical arts, crafting ingenious devices to defend themselves when danger comes.

zh:
走夜路的人，有时会遇到一排穿着红衣服默默行走的小女孩。打头那个看着最可怜，总爱跟路人伸手央求：“牵我走一段吧，我怕黑。”
有个晚归的货郎，看领头那红衣丫头实在可怜，就牵了她的手。这一牵却发现，那双手如同铁箍，冰凉刺骨，甩都甩不开！货郎吓得魂飞魄散，想跑，脚却不听使唤，只能跟着那队红衣女孩走。
她们越走越快，专挑没人的荒林子里钻。货郎想喊，喉咙像被堵住一样。他惊恐地发现，自己的手也开始发青发冷，再看那些女孩，个个眼神空洞，哪有一点小孩样？最后，他竟迷迷糊糊排进了队伍末尾，骨头像是被打断，也成了个穿红衣服的女孩，跟着走，眼神也渐渐空了。
老人说，那是被“牵”进去的替死鬼。领头那丫头的手，就是勾魂索，牵上了就得顶她的缺，永世跟着走。
en:
Nightward travelers sometimes cross paths with a silent procession of little girls garbed in blood-red. The vanguard of this macabre troupe appears the most wretched, forever reaching out to wayfarers with a trembling beg: "Walk with me a while. The dark frightens me."
A late-returning peddler, blinded by misplaced mercy, took the leading girl's hand. Instantly, he found her grip to be a shackle of freezing iron, impossible to cast off. His soul fractured with terror. He willed himself to flee, yet his legs betrayed him, forcing him to march in step with the crimson procession.
Their pace quickened, diving into the most barren, sunless thickets. He tried to cry for help, but his throat was sealed as if packed with grave-dirt. In mounting horror, he watched his own flesh turn a bruised, lifeless blue. He gazed at the girls, their eyes were vacuous pits, bereft of all humanity. At last, his mind clouded. His bones snapped and contorted until he took his place at the rear of the line: another girl in a red dress, marching silently into the gloom, his own eyes now hollow voids.
The old ones call them the replacement spirits, drawn in by the clasp. The first girl's hand is a soul-snaring noose. Clasp it, and you fill her vacancy, doomed to wander the dark forever.

前路茫茫，不知来日所向，亦不知平生所为何用。

en:
I entered the Inkbound Order at the age of seven. When the great disaster struck, I took up my master's dying wish, dedicating my life to safeguarding our ancient texts and keeping our lineage alive.
But as war tore through the land, the world was plunged into decades of darkness. A single pillar cannot support a falling sky.
Now, my friends have all faded away, and my own days are numbered.
The road ahead is bleak. I don't know what the future holds, nor if my life's work meant anything in the end.
If an era of peace finally dawns, I beg any kindred spirit from a future generation to tell me in my dreams.
If I could just hear that news, I would gladly be reborn just to see that peace with my own eyes.

zh:
皎皎随信送来鞋子的时候，他跳了起来，桌角撞到了膝盖。
时隔多年，他又穿上了女儿做的鞋子。那双鞋针脚细腻，只是尺寸有些宽松。

傍晚，他瘫在宴会的角落，那个叫小盘的女孩悄悄过来的时候，鞋子的后跟就掉了。
他在宴会混战中朝方白冲去。他们这对“翁婿”不久前才见了一面。此时绝地当中，他们又对视了一眼。就这一眼，他们决定赌一把。方白藏贤掌法袭来，他微微收了收身。掌风击中他，而不是击穿了他。他变成在角落里的一具不起眼的“尸体”，不会有人知道，或者关心他还有一口气。他和方白赌赢了，但那双鞋彻底掉了。

被仆人当尸体抬出去的时候，他模模糊糊地可惜，直到从尸体堆里爬出来，还在念念不忘。
没了鞋子，原本好好的路也跟他做对，被掉落的巨石堵住了。那石头真不识趣，他使劲推啊拍啊，都纹丝不动。
他只觉得气愤，想着，要是那双鞋还在就好了。

一双好的鞋，能让他抓着地。面前这封路的石头还是自己年轻时半掌就打碎的添头，怎么就推不开了呢？
受了点子伤，没力气了，连手也变小了吗？

哦他知道了，原来人老了，就像做鞋的布一样，会缩水。皎皎给他做了那么多次鞋子，不是这次做大了。是他，变矮小了。
他年轻时，妻子一眼就相中了他，身材高大。妻子死后，他背着女儿四处奔波，女儿也常说爹爹就像山一样。
但现在这山，怎么变成小土包了呢？
他拍打着巨石，一次又一次地拍打着。这一生有很多事情从他身边闪过。他置之不理。直到想起了很早之前的那一幕。

他抱着年幼的女儿去求医，那武林名宿的山门紧紧闭着。他等了很久，甚至一瞬间，膝盖就要跪下去。
当时他跪了吗？有什么让他犹豫了吗？膝盖在疼，是皎皎在叫他吗？皎皎当时说什么来着？
兰守持一边想着，一边拍打着巨石。他想到了，小盘转述的就是皎皎当年那句话啊。皎皎说——
“我的爹爹是惊涛掌，是这世间一等一的大英雄。”
“他、咳咳、他才不要跪你们！”
兰守持直起身子，又一掌，拍了出去。
皎皎说，我是大英雄呐。
巨石裂开。
半掌惊涛，重现江湖。

在无人在意的尸体堆里。
在即将被淹没的桃林塞。

风浪掀起来了，但他是惊涛掌。
en:
When Jiaojiao's parcel arrived with the shoes inside, he actually leapt up—hard enough to bang his knee against the table. 
After so many years, he was wearing something made by his daughter again. The stitching was fine as silk, but the fit—just a little loose. 

That evening, when he was slumped in a dim corner of the banquet, the heel slipped off just as the girl called Xiaopan edged toward him. 
Then the hall erupted. Through the chaos, he charged straight at Fang Bai. The two of them—future in‑laws who had met only once—locked eyes in the middle of that desperate moment. And in that single glance, they both decided to gamble. Fang Bai's Sage Palm swept toward him. He shifted back just a hair. The blow struck him, but didn't pierce through. He crumpled into a nameless heap in the corner—one more "corpse" no one would check, no one would mourn. Their gamble paid off. But his shoes were gone. 

Carried out with the dead, he drifted in and out, dimly grieving the loss. Even after he crawled out of the corpse pile, he was still thinking about them. 
Without those shoes, even a clear path betrayed him—blocked by a massive fallen rock. The thing sat there, shameless as a stubborn mule. He pushed, he slapped, he shoved with all the breath he had left. It didn't move an inch. 
Anger rose hot in his chest. If only he still had those shoes. 

A good pair lets a man find his footing. And this boulder—this lump—was nothing more than a scrap from his youth, a stone he could once shatter with half a palm. So why couldn't he budge it now? 
He must be hurt. Weakened. Had his hands... gotten smaller? 

And then it dawned on him. Age shrinks a man, the same way cloth shrinks when shoes are made. Jiaojiao had sewn for him so many times—it wasn't her stitching that had grown too large. He was the one who had grown small. 
When he was young, his wife had fallen for him at a single glance—broad‑shouldered, tall, unshakable. After she died, he carried his daughter from city to city in search of cures. She used to say her father was like a mountain. 
But now—when had that mountain crumbled into a small hill? 
He struck the boulder again and again. A lifetime of memories rushed past him. None stopped—Until one did. 

He remembered carrying little Jiaojiao to seek help from a famed master. The gates were locked tight. He waited so long that his knees nearly gave way to the dirt. 
But had he knelt? What held him back? His knees had hurt—was Jiaojiao calling him? What had she said? 
Lan Shouchi pounded the rock, searching the past. And suddenly he knew. The words Xiaopan had repeated earlier were the very ones Jiaojiao had said back then: 
"My father is the Palm Master Fierceness—the greatest hero in the world." 
"He—*cough, cough*—he'll never kneel to the likes of you!" 
Lan Shouchi straightened. He drew back his arm and struck. 
Jiaojiao said I'm a great hero. 
The boulder split. 
Half‑Palm Against the Tide—returned to the jianghu. 

In a heap of bodies no one looked at. 
In Peach Grove Pass about to drown. 

The waves were rising high—but he was Palm Master Fierceness.

zh:
黄河边的雨，同开封别处的雨不同。
有人说：雨是河伯的泪，因被困在黄河千千万万年，所以一哭，就停不下来。
从不见山南下的雀，听了觉得有趣：呼风唤雨的河伯莫非只是个娃娃，受了委屈便要哭哭啼啼。
否则，又怎会多出黄河边这许多风雨？

雀打小就不爱哭哭啼啼，因为“哭”打不败山匪、填不饱肚子、医不好寒症，是天底下最无用的东西，而天底下最有用的，不过自己的双手而已。伤痛难忍，便采药以疗，饥肠饿肚，便攀采野蔬、手搏山兽。流离失所，家中无房无室，便入不见山拜师习艺，为瘸父瞎母成天下第一之屋室。那一天前，雀一直相信，只要自己动手，便没有什么是办不成的，直至屋室完工之时……医馆的小郎中冒冒失失地跑过来：“阿雀，你爹娘……没挺过去……”

原来有些事，并非人力所能及，一切似乎只看天意。当日，雀将爹娘葬于新家，向南走去，身后遮天的火，将一切吞噬。原来，人是天地中那么渺小的存在，便是竭尽全力，也不能撼动天地分毫。如此，人要往何处去，营营所学，又是为何？“连话本里呼风唤雨的神明河伯，也要为了这止不住的黄河水哭哭啼啼啊。”早被雨淋湿的雀，自嘲地想。

可是，天上的风雨却在此刻停了。
眼前是一道红色的身影：“喂，你都湿透了，和我一起回家吧。”
en:
The rain by the Yellow River was unlike the rain anywhere else in Kaifeng.
Some said the rain was the tears of the River Master, trapped in the Yellow River for millennia, crying endlessly.
Que from the Bujian Hill, hearing this tale, found it amusing: how could the mighty River Master, who could summon wind and rain, be like a child, wailing at the slightest grievance?
Otherwise, how else would there be such relentless storms along the Yellow River?

But Que had never been one to cry. Crying couldn't defeat mountain bandits, fill an empty stomach, or cure a lingering illness. To the sparrow, crying was the most useless thing in the world. The most useful? Her own two hands. When pain was unbearable, she gathered herbs to heal herself. When hunger gnawed at her, she foraged wild plants and hunted animals. When her family was homeless, she apprenticed to a craftsman in Hidden Mountain, learning to build the best houses in the land for her crippled father and blind mother. She believed, up until the day their home was completed, that there was nothing her hands couldn't accomplish. But then, the young doctor from the clinic came running: "A'que, your parents... they didn't make it."

Some things, she realized, were beyond human effort. It all seemed to depend on fate. That day, she buried her parents by the new house and walked southward. Behind her, flames engulfed everything. Men were so small in the grand scheme of things, powerless to move the heavens or earth, no matter how hard they tried. So, where should one go? What was the point of all her skills? "Even the River Master, who can summon storms in the tales, can't stop the Yellow River from weeping," she thought bitterly, drenched in rain.

But at that moment, the storm ceased.
Before her stood a figure in red. "Hey, you're soaked. Come home with me."
Leather Wine Gourd
Half-Awake in the Cold

zh:
杠之一道虽毒，然吾辈岂能畏之。
吾四人于文士一道略有所得，受世人追捧，忝为人四大家，自当以身为则，为天下寻抑杠之法，遂得上中下三策以为注，望后人鉴之。
下策曰，力击之。杠之道虽利，终为言之术。然胜负不唯言之一道，事不可为当不惧以力证之。此策终难服众，顾曰下策。
中策曰，且听之。杠之道虽毒，然无欲则无伤。言者因是非而辩，无是则无非，若清风过岗，去留无意。然此策仅可自保，顾曰中策。
上策曰，理辩之。杠之道虽诡，却失之以理。天下之辩皆出于理，若人人明理，则杠之道若无根之木，不攻自破。
<似乎还有一行小字>
虽有上中下策，然人心浮动。世人追捧名士，争相效之，仅杠之一字即可与名士争锋，有此终南捷径，又岂甘埋首苦读？惜之，惜之……
en:
Arguing can be toxic, but are we, the Four Silver Tongues, to shy away? Esteemed as masters of rhetoric, it is our duty to lead by example and offer three strategies to counter sophistry: lower, middle, and upper.
The Lower Strategy: Respond with force. Though clever words can win battles, not every dispute must be settled by speech alone. If reason fails, one may answer with strength. Yet this rarely convinces others, and so it is the lowest method.
The Middle Strategy: Ignore it. Sophistry may sting, but if you remain unmoved, you cannot be harmed. Let arguments pass like wind over the hills, indifferent and untouched. This preserves yourself, but changes little. Hence, the middle way.
The Upper Strategy: Reason with it. Sophistry may twist words, but it cannot stand against true logic. If all understand reason, empty arguments fall apart on their own. This is the highest approach.
(A line of tiny script follows)
Yet even with these strategies, hearts remain restless. The world admires eloquent speakers, eager to imitate them. If one can rival the famous simply by clever arguing, why toil in true study? What a pity...

zh:
凉州有荒墟，曰藤王村。其地阴壑潜通，每至夜分则雪坼无辍。村中古藤虬曲若苍龙，霜皮斑驳，世传藤王枝生“藤王葡萄”，实如冰魄，酿汁成浆，色若琥珀，昔年胡商以百金易一瓮，狂澜侠客解刀换醉，倾囊之声不绝于坊市。
自安史兵燹，膏腴之地尽化蒿莱。今过其墟，唯见颓垣间鬼火明灭。子夜风起，枯藤忽绽莹蓝葡萄，大如鸡子，然晓光初露即萎。
尝有异人云：此乃鬼民执念所化。彼等不知身死，夜夜培土剪枝，欲复葡萄宴旧观。然纵结鬼果千筐，终难破阴阳之锢。寒鸡一唱，唯余蔓草间碎杯映月，泠泠如泪。
en:
There is a ruin in Liangzhou called Kingvine Village. Hidden valleys crisscross beneath it. Every night, the sound of cracking ice echoes endlessly. Ancient vines in the village twist like black dragons, their frost-covered bark mottled. Legend has it that the "Kingvine Grape" grows on the vines, its fruit as clear as ice, its juice brewed into a liquid as amber-colored as honey. In the past, foreign merchants traded a hundred taels of gold for a jar, chivalrous swordsmen exchanged their blades for a drink, and the sound of emptied purses filled the markets. 
Since the Anshi rebellion's flames of war, fertile lands turned to weeds. Now passing the ruins, one sees only will-o'-wisps flickering among crumbling walls. At midnight, wind rises, and the withered vines suddenly bloom with glowing blue grapes, large as chicken eggs, yet they wither at the first light of dawn. 
Once a stranger said that this was formed from the ghost folk's obsession. Unaware of their own deaths, they till soil and prune branches night after night, trying to restore the former spectacle of the grape feast. Yet even if a thousand baskets of ghost fruit are borne, they cannot break the barrier between yin and yang. When the cold rooster crows, only shattered cups among the vines reflect the moon, cold and clear as tears.

zh:
多年以后，面对墨城野外满地走的大鹅队伍，我仍能想起鸽子飞来的那一天。
我知道这只鸽子带来的是师门大宴的邀请，可此刻我究竟是要开窗让鸽子进来，还是要闭窗当作没见过这只鸽？
如墨子所言，城郭不备全，不可以自守。心无备虑，不可以应卒。
因此每当我面临重大人生决策，我便把心中的芜杂思绪悉数记下，说不定答案自会浮出水面。

猜想一：
若我赴宴，长老定当笑靥如花，举杯相迎。同门师兄妹亦会围炉而坐，把酒言欢，共叙墨城风云，畅谈野心壮志。然酒过三巡，或有好事者起身出题论道。有道是言无务为多而务为智，无务为文而务为察。若我言为智，从此同门之间又多了一段佳话。可若我言多则失，学术地位必会下降，说不定至少半年都会被此难题所困扰，郁郁寡欢……

猜想二：
若我不赴，长老定会眉头紧锁，心中暗叹。同门师兄妹亦会私下议论，说我架子颇大，不顾同门之情。可我却能借此机会抢占过于火热的悬空屋，闭关研发最新机巧。或许在深山之中，灵感涌现，从此发明无阻，终成新一代机巧大师。亦或误入歧途，走火入魔，即便延期毕业也无货可交。然而，若我故意不去，长老或会心生不满，日后相见或有诸多不便……

猜想三：
若我总徘徊于赴与不赴之间，犹豫不决，可能最终即未能与长老同门共聚，又未能专心于机巧研发。此题难解！过度思考易心生苦闷，更易脱发。此刻真想独自痛饮，说不定酒过三巡之后，心生豪情，自会决定明日赴宴与否……且慢，说起饮酒，若能有一只烧鸽相佐更为美妙……

哦！或许最美的答案，已在鸽与不鸽之中自动浮现，真真是“力，刑之所以奋也”……
en:
Years later, facing the gaggle of geese roaming the Mohist City wilds, I would still remember that afternoon when the pigeon first arrived.
I knew it carried an invitation to the sect feast. But at that moment, should I open the window and let it in, or pretend I never saw it?
"An ill-fortified city cannot defend itself; an unprepared mind cannot face the unexpected." Whenever I face big decisions, I jot down all my tangled thoughts, hoping clarity will come.

Option one:
If I go, the elders will greet me warmly, and fellow disciples will gather around the fire, sharing stories and ambitions. Yet someone will likely challenge me with a tough question. If I respond wisely, it could become a celebrated story; but if I stumble, my reputation may suffer, and I'll be stuck obsessing over it for months.

Option two:
If I skip the feast, the elders will be disappointed, and others might call me arrogant. But I'd have the Aloft Abode to focus on invention. Perhaps I'd find inspiration in solitude and become a master artisan, or maybe I'd lose my way and fail to graduate on time. Also, refusing the invitation might sour future relations with the elders.

Option three:
Caught in the dilemma, I risk losing both the feast and focus on my work. A frustrating limbo. At times like that, I just want to drink alone, hoping a few cups will give me the resolve to decide. Wait... speaking of wine, wouldn't it be divine if a certain pigeon were roasted to go with it?

Maybe the best answer lies somewhere between. The very act of wrestling with the choice is what gives me strength.

黎蓁蓁不恨那些追杀的人。
她为了报恩杀了他们的亲友，他们自然也可以为了复仇来杀她。
江湖上的事，都是一报还一报，有人报恩，有人报仇，生死偿命。
唯一遗憾的，是偿命的这一天，来得太早了些。
早到她还没有来得及整理好行囊，与那个人一同往南。

她这辈子，是很多人。
是神秘莫测的剑客月神，是杀尽义士的奸邪之辈，是独守秘密的人，是欠债的人。
但生命的最后，她谁都不想做了。
她只想做她自己。
原原本本的黎蓁蓁。
就像她种的那些花儿。

拜月之花，生于泥泞，不见万物，仍向月而拜、听风而眠。
若有下一世，便让她做一朵花吧。
en:
Li Zhenzhen doesn't hate those who come after her.
After all, she has taken the lives of their loved ones to settle a debt, and so they have every right to seek revenge.
In this world, everything was settled with a balance of blood. Some debts were repaid with kindness, others with vengeance.
Life and death were always a transaction.
Her only regret is that the moment of death comes too soon.
She couldn't pack her things and leave for the South with that man.

Throughout her life, she has had many roles.
She is the elusive swordswoman, the Lunar Goddess; she is the villain who slaughtered warriors; she is the keeper of secrets, the one forever in debt.
But when it comes to the end of it all, she doesn't want to be any of these things.
She simply wants to be herself.
The untainted Li Zhenzhen.
Much like the flowers she planted.

The Moonflower, born from the mud, unnoticed by the world, yet still bowing to the moon and sleeping with the wind.
If there is a next life, she hopes to be nothing more than a flower.

zh:
青少年时期，和她的师父鹤一样爱写日记。青的人情债。此时的风格也很活泼。
扉页写着：下次一定，必不迟到。（而内页全是迟到日常）
写着自己的咕咕日常，在某次刷刀时察觉到自己的真气可以随着武器延伸很远，颇为自得；& 因为咕咕而计划给张万师和鸦的补偿。（后续信息会展示，大部分补偿未能实现，到最后都被鸦惦记着）
（比如某次计划给鸦补偿是一个绣了一半的飞鸟帕子，手法粗糙，看轮廓是很胖一个青黑色的鸟。实在拿不出手，可后来这帕子却找不见了。（被鸦收藏了）
（给张万师的补偿是山外收集的水利古籍原本，结果路上遇见山匪，打斗中把古籍切作两半。又实在拿不出手，便决意誊抄一份给张万师，仅抄了个开头，师兄便出山了……后诸事繁忙，这抄了一半的书册便搁置了）
（倒是挥剑削成的一朴拙竹簪子，鹤很是喜欢，常常用来挽发，她的手艺，也就用剑能做到的那些才拿得出手了。
en:
In her youth, like her master Crane, she loved keeping a diary. Halcyon's debt of gratitude. The style at this time was also very lively.
The flyleaf read: Next time for sure, absolutely not late. (But the inside pages were all about being late daily)
She wrote about her daily procrastination, once feeling quite proud when she realized her Qi could extend far along her weapon; & planned compensations for Zhang Wanshi and Raven due to her lateness. (Subsequent information shows most compensations were not realized, and in the end, Raven still remembered them)
(For example, once planned to compensate Raven with a half-embroidered bird handkerchief, rough in craftsmanship, showing a very fat, dark blue-black bird. Too embarrassing to give it, but later she found the handkerchief missing. (Collected by Raven))(Craner compensation for Zhang Wanshi was an original manuscript of a water conservancy classic collected outside the mountains. On the way, she encountered mountain bandits and accidentally cut the book in half during the fight. Too embarrassing to give it, she decided to copy a version for Zhang Wanshi. She only copied the beginning before her senior brother left the mountains... Later, busy with various matters, the half-copied book was put aside.)
(However, a simple bamboo hairpin she carved with her sword was greatly loved by Crane, who often used it to tie up his hair. Craner craftsmanship was only really good enough for the things she could do with her sword.)

【雍也第六】

子曰：“雍也，可使南面也。仲弓问子桑伯子。”子曰：“可也，简。”仲弓曰：“居敬而行简，以临其民，不亦可乎？居简而行简，无乃太简乎？”子曰：“雍之言然。”
哀公问曰：“弟子孰为好学？”孔子对曰：“有颜回者好学，不迁怒，不贰过，不幸短命死矣。今也则亡，未闻好学者也。”
子华使于齐，冉子为其母请粟，子曰：“与之釜。”请益，曰：“与之庾。”冉子与之粟五秉。子曰：“赤之适齐也，乘肥马，衣轻裘。吾闻之也：君子周急不继富。”
原思为之宰，与之粟九百，辞。子曰：“毋，以与尔邻里乡党乎？”
子谓仲弓曰：“犁牛之子骍且角，虽欲勿用，山川其舍诸？”
子曰：“回也，其心三月不违仁，其余则日月至焉而已矣。”
季康子问：“仲由可使从政也与？”子曰：“由也果，于从政乎何有？曰：“赐也可使从政也与？”子曰：“赐也达，于从政乎何有？”曰：“求也可使从政也与？”子曰：“求也艺，于从政乎何有？”
季氏使闵子骞为费宰，闵子骞曰：“善为我辞焉。如有复我者，则吾必在汶上矣。”
伯牛有疾，子问之，自牖执其手，曰：“亡之，命矣夫！斯人也而有斯疾也。斯人也而有斯疾也。”
子曰：“贤哉，回也！一箪食，一瓢饮，在陋巷，人不堪其忧，回也不改其乐，贤哉，回也！”
冉有曰：“非不说子之道也，力不足也。”子曰：“力不足者，中道而废，今女画。”
子谓子夏曰：“为君子儒，毋为小人儒。”
子游为武城宰。子曰：“女得人焉耳乎哉？”曰：“有澹台灭明者，行不由径，非公事，未尝至于偃之室也。”
子曰：“孟之反不伐，奔而殿，将入门，策其马，曰：‘非敢后也，马不进也。’”
子曰：“不有祝𬶍之佞，而有宋朝之美，难乎免于今之世矣。”
子曰：“谁能出不由户者？何莫由斯道也？”
子曰：“质胜文则野，文胜质则史。文质彬彬，然后君子。”
子曰：“人之生也直，罔之生也幸而免。”
子曰：“知者不如好之者，好之者不如乐之者。”
子曰：“中人以上，可以语上也；中人以下，不可以语上也。”
樊迟问知，子曰：“务民之义，敬鬼神而远之，可谓知矣。”问仁，子曰：“仁者先难而后获，可谓仁矣。”
子曰：“知者乐水，仁者乐山。知者动，仁者静。知者乐，仁者寿。”
子曰：“齐一变，至于鲁。 鲁一变，至于道。”
子曰：“觚不觚，觚哉！觚哉！”
宰我问曰：“仁者，虽告之曰：‘井有仁者焉。’其从之也？”子曰：“何为其然也？君子可逝也，不可陷也；可欺也，不可罔也。”
子曰：“君子博学于文，约之以礼，亦可以弗畔矣夫。”
子见南子，子路不说，夫子矢之曰：“予所否者，天厌之！天厌之！”
子曰：“中庸之为德也，其至矣乎！民鲜久矣。”
子贡曰：“如能博施于民而能济众者，何如？可谓仁乎？”子曰：“何事于仁？必也圣乎！尧、舜其犹病诸！夫仁者，己欲立而立人，己欲达而达人。能近取譬，可谓仁之方也已。”
en:
[Chapter 6: Yong]

The Master said, "There is Yong! He might occupy the place of a prince." Zhonggong asked about Zisang Bozi. The Master said, "He may pass. He does not mind small matters." Zhonggong said, "If one cherish in oneself a reverential feeling of the necessity of attention to business, though one may be easy in small matters, in one's government of the people, that may be allowed. But if one cherish in oneself that easy feeling, and also carry it out in one's practice, is not such an easy mode of procedure excessive?" The Master said, "Yong's words are right."
Duke Ai asked which of the disciples loved to learn. Confucius replied to him, "There was Yan Hui; he loved to learn. He did not transfer his anger; he did not repeat a fault. Unfortunately, his appointed time was short and he died; and now there is not such another. I have not yet heard of anyone who loves to learn as he did."
Zihua being employed on a mission to Qi, the disciple Ran requested grain for his mother. The Master said, "Give her a fu." Ran requested more. "Give her a yu," said the Master. Ran gave her five bing. The Master said, "When Chi was proceeding to Qi, he had fat horses to his carriage, and wore light furs. I have heard that a superior person helps the distressed, but does not add to the wealth of the rich."
Yuan Si being made governor of his town by the Master, he gave him nine hundred measures of grain, but Si declined them. The Master said, "Do not decline them. May you not give them away in the neighbourhoods, hamlets, towns, and villages?"
The Master, speaking of Zhonggong, said, "If the calf of a brindled cow be red and horned, although one may not wish to use it, would the spirits of the mountains and rivers put it aside?"
The Master said, "Such was Hui that for three months there would be nothing in his mind contrary to perfect virtue. The others may attain to this on some days or in some months, but nothing more."
Ji Kang asked, "Is Zhongyou fit to be employed as an officer of government?" The Master said, "You is a person of decision; what difficulty would he find in being an officer of government?" Kang asked, "Is Ci fit to be employed as an officer of government?" and was answered, "Ci is a person of intelligence; what difficulty would he find in being an officer of government?" And to the same question about Qiu the Master gave the same reply, saying, "Qiu is a person of various ability."
The chief of the Ji family sent to ask Min Ziqian to be governor of Bi. Min Ziqian said, "Decline the offer for me politely. If anyone come again to me with a second invitation, I shall be obliged to go and live on the banks of the Wen."
Boniu being sick, the Master went to ask for him. He took hold of his hand through the window, and said, "It is killing him. It is the appointment of Heaven, alas! That such a person should have such a sickness! That such a person should have such a sickness!"
The Master said, "Admirable indeed was the virtue of Hui! With a single bamboo dish of rice, a single gourd dish of drink, and living in his mean narrow lane, while others could not have endured the distress, he did not allow his joy to be affected by it. Admirable indeed was the virtue of Hui!"
Ran Qiu said, "It is not that I do not delight in your doctrines, but my strength is insufficient." The Master said, "Those whose strength is insufficient give over in the middle of the way, but now you limit yourself."
The Master said to Zixia, "Do you be a scholar after the style of the superior person, and not after that of the mean person."
Ziyou being governor of Wucheng, the Master said to him, "Have you got good people there?" He answered, "There is Tantai Mieming, who never in walking takes a short cut, and never comes to my office, excepting on public business."
The Master said, "Meng Zhifan does not boast of his merit. Being in the rear on an occasion of flight, when they were about to enter the gate, he whipped up his horse saying, 'It is not that I dare to be last. My horse would not advance.'"
The Master said, "Without the specious speech of the litanist Tuo, and the beauty of the prince Zhao of Song, it is difficult to escape in the present age."
The Master said, "Who can go out but by the door? How is it that people will not walk according to these ways?"
The Master said, "Where the solid qualities are in excess of accomplishments, we have rusticity; where the accomplishments are in excess of the solid qualities, we have the manners of a clerk. When the accomplishments and solid qualities are equally blended, we then have the person of complete virtue."
The Master said, "One is born for uprightness. If one lose one's uprightness, and yet live, one's escape from death is the effect of mere good fortune."
The Master said, "They who know the truth are not equal to those who love it, and they who love it are not equal to those who find pleasure in it."
The Master said, "To those whose talents are above mediocrity, the highest subjects may be announced. To those who are below mediocrity, the highest subjects may not be announced."
Fan Chi asked what constituted wisdom. The Master said, "To give oneself earnestly to the duties due to people, and, while respecting spiritual beings, to keep aloof from them, may be called wisdom." He asked about perfect virtue. The Master said, "The person of virtue makes the difficulty to be overcome one's first business, and success only a subsequent consideration—this may be called perfect virtue."
The Master said, "The wise find pleasure in water; the virtuous find pleasure in hills. The wise are active; the virtuous are tranquil. The wise are joyful, the virtuous are long-lived."
The Master said, "Qi, by one change, would come to the state of Lu. Lu, by one change, would come to a state where true principles predominated."
The Master said, "A cornered vessel without corners—A strange cornered vessel! A strange cornered vessel!"
Zai Wo asked, saying, "A benevolent person, though it be told one, 'There is a person in the well,' will go in after that person, I suppose." Confucius said, "Why should one do so? A superior person may be made to go to the well, but one cannot be made to go down into it. One may be imposed upon, but one cannot be befooled."
The Master said, "The superior person, extensively studying all learning, and keeping oneself under the restraint of the rules of propriety, may thus likewise not overstep what is right."
The Master having visited Nanzi, Zilu was displeased, on which the Master swore, saying, "Wherein I have done improperly, may Heaven reject me! May Heaven reject me!"
The Master said, "Perfect is the virtue which is according to the Constant Mean! Rare for a long time has been its practice among the people."
Zigong said, "Suppose the case of a person extensively conferring benefits on the people, and able to assist all, what would you say of one? Might one be called perfectly virtuous?" The Master said, "Why speak only of virtue in connection with one? Must one not have the qualities of a sage? Even Yao and Shun were still solicitous about this. Now the person of perfect virtue, wishing to be established oneself, seeks also to establish others; wishing to be enlarged oneself, seeks also to enlarge others. To be able to judge of others by what is nigh in ourselves—this may be called the art of virtue."

zh: 相传宋太祖赵匡胤曾于建隆三年（962年）秘密刻制石碑，立于皇宫寝殿密室之中。其上有三条誓约：立誓保全后周柴氏宗室；保全士大夫及上书议政的言官；赵氏子孙若不遵循上述两条誓言，将遭天谴。
en:
Legend says that Zhao Kuangyin, Emperor Taizu of Song, had a stone stele secretly carved in Jianlong, Year 3 (962) and placed in a hidden chamber within the palace sleeping quarters.

It is said to bear three vows:
1. To protect the Later Zhou Chai clan.
2. To safeguard the scholar-officials, including remonstrating officials who submitted memorials and debated state affairs.
3. If the Zhao descendants failed to uphold the first two vows, they would incur Heaven's wrath.

zh: “伏以田宏正首变魏俗，彰先帝之睿谋；近入镇州，宣陛下神武。积成忠恳，大有勋劳，人怀去思，愿刻金石。陛下所宜外诏台席，内委翰林，妙选雄文，式扬丕绩。岂谓天光曲照，御札特书，猥付微臣，实非常例。臣顷以特恩拔擢，便欲效死仰酬，遂竭愚诚，累蒙召对。自去年九月已后，横遭谤毁，无由再睹天颜，分随枯朽而凋，永绝恩波之望。岂料圣慈长在，记忆姓名，无人奏请撰碑，便自宸衷宣付。微臣忝非木石，粗有肺肠，空怀感涕之心，未获杀身之所。无任感恩思报镂骨铭肌之至。”
en: "Tian Hongzheng was the first to reform the customs of Wei, manifesting the late emperor's wisdom. Recently, he entered Zhenzhou, displaying Your Majesty's divine might. His accumulated loyalty and monumental achievements have left a lasting legacy, and the people, remembering his deeds, wished to carve them in stone. Your Majesty should have commanded the court scholars or entrusted the Hanlin Academy to select a masterful text to glorify his deeds. Yet unexpectedly, the imperial brush personally assigned this humble servant, an extraordinary honor. I was once specially promoted by grace and wished to repay it with my life, exhausting my sincerity in repeated audiences. But since last September, slander has barred me from seeing the imperial countenance again, resigned to wither like dead wood, cut off from the flow of imperial favor. Who could have imagined the Emperor's enduring kindness, remembering my name? None petitioned for me to compose this stele. It came directly from the imperial will. I am no block of wood, nor without heart; though I have longed to express my gratitude, I have found no means to sacrifice myself. My indebtedness is carved into my bones and flesh."

这本应是寻常人避之不及的所在，然而不知为何，青溪、无心谷、绣金楼的人在得知消息后，却纷纷赶赴此地，又因不同的目的而展开争斗。
于是渐渐地，江湖上出现流言。说隐雾林中有一医家秘宝，可以令人起死回生、长生不老。无数江湖人因此深入林中，甘冒九死一生之险，只为寻找传说中的宝藏。可他们的结局却往往是出师未捷身先死，最后沦为这段传奇中无足轻重的一笔感叹。
en:
The Mistveil Forest in southeastern Kaifeng lies perpetually cloaked in mist and miasma, its depths riddled with hidden perils and strange poisons.
The dreaded Dawn-to-Dusk plague, once a scourge upon the land, now roams unchecked within. Though most avoid this cursed place, word has drawn disciples of Silver Needle, Hollow Vale, and the Aureate Pavilion, each pursuing their own designs.
Whispers spread through the jianghu that a peerless treasure lies within the Mistveil Forest, a relic said to raise the dead and grant immortality. Lured by such promise, countless wanderers have braved the forest, only to vanish into its shadows, their names fading into mere footnotes in the legend.

zh:
【地理·三】

【泉】

宿业师山房，期丁大不至
孟浩然
夕阳度西岭，群壑倏已暝。
松月生夜凉，风泉满清听。
樵人归欲尽，烟鸟栖初定。
之子期宿来，孤琴候萝径。

游南阳清泠泉
李白
惜彼落日暮，爱此寒泉清。
西辉逐流水，荡漾游子情。
空歌望云月，曲尽长松声。

日暮
杜甫
牛羊下来久，各已闭柴门。
风月自清夜，江山非故园。
石泉流暗壁，草露滴秋根。
头白灯明里，何须花烬繁。

【海】

春日望海
李世民
披襟眺沧海，凭轼玩春芳。
积流横地纪，疏派引天潢。
仙气凝三岭，和风扇八荒。
拂潮云布色，穿浪日舒光。
照岸花分彩，迷云雁断行。
怀卑运深广，持满守灵长。
有形非易测，无源讵可量。
洪涛经变野，翠岛屡成桑。
之罘思汉帝，碣石想秦皇。
霓裳非本意，端拱是图王。

送秘书晁监还日本国
王维
积水不可极，安知沧海东。
九州何处远，万里若乘空。
向国唯看日，归帆但信风。
鳌身映天黑，鱼眼射波红。
乡树扶桑外，主人孤岛中。
别离方异域，音信若为通。

有所思
李白
我思仙人，乃在碧海之东隅。
海寒多天风，白波连山倒蓬壶。
长鲸喷涌不可涉，抚心茫茫泪如珠。
西来青鸟东飞去，愿寄一书谢麻姑。

浪淘沙
白居易
一泊沙来一泊去，一重浪灭一重生。
相搅相淘无歇日，会交山海一时平。
白浪茫茫与海连，平沙浩浩四无边。
暮去朝来淘不住，遂令东海变桑田。
借问江湖与海水，何似君情与妾心。
相恨不如潮有信，相思始觉海非深。
en:
【Geography · III】

【Spring】

Awaiting in Vain a Friend in the Mountain
Meng Haoran
The sun has sunk behind the western hill,
In every valley twilight reigns so still.
The moon among the pines makes night more cool,
In breeze I hear the murmuring of a pool.
Woodcutters are going home one by one,
In mist-veiled trees birds settle down, their songs done.
Waiting for you to come and pass the night,
With lonely lute I stay on the vine-roofed way.

The Clear and Cool Spring in Nanyang
Li Bai
I love the clear and cool spring,
And regret the setting sun.
Westward glow chases running stream,
Stirring the heart of a roamer.
In vain I sing to cloud and moon,
My song ends in the pines' long tune.

Dusk
Du Fu
Long have sheep and cows come down from the hill,
And each house has closed its wicker gate.
Wind and moon make a clear night still,
But hills and streams are not my native state.
From dark cliff the fountain flows unseen,
On autumn roots drips dew from grass so green.
In lamplight I see my hair turn white,
What's the use of sparks from wick so bright?

【Sea】

Gazing at the Sea in Spring
Li Shimin
I open my coat to gaze at the blue sea,
Leaning on the carriage, I enjoy spring's glee.
Accumulated streams cross the earth's frame,
Diverted branches lead to the heavenly drain.
Immortal air congeals on three hills high,
Gentle breeze fans the eight wastes far and nigh.
Clouds dye the tide with color as they sweep,
The sunbeams pierce the waves, their rays leap.
Flowers on shore vie in splendor bright,
Wild geese lost in clouds break their flight.
Humble, it runs deep and wide,
Full, it keeps its spirit's pride.
Its form is hard to measure,
Its source is beyond treasure.
Great waves have changed fields to the sea,
Green isles have turned to mulberry.
At Zhifu I think of the Han Emperor's might,
At Jieshi, of the First Emperor's sight.
Rainbow dress was not my real will,
To rule with folded arms is my skill.

Farewell to Secretary Chao Back to Japan
Wang Wei
Boundless the ocean seems to be,
Who knows where lies the Eastern Sea?
Far, far away the land of your birth,
You'll go as if you'd skyward fly.
To find your home you'll watch the sun,
And trust your ship to winds that blow.
The giant turtle darkens the sky,
The monstrous fish makes red waves glow.
Your homeland's trees lie far away,
Your master's on an isle, they say.
We'll part to live in different lands;
How can we send word to each other?

Thinking of Someone
Li Bai
I think of the fair one in eastern sea,
Where cold wind blows and white waves rise like hills.
I cannot cross the sea where whales spout free,
My heart's so sad that tears my bosom fills.
The blue bird from the west eastward will fly;
I'd ask it to bring you a word from me.

Waves Scouring Sand
Bai Juyi
Wave on wave, the sand comes and goes;
One wave dies, another grows.
They wash and cleanse each other day by day,
Till mountains crumble and seas turn into clay.
The boundless sea merges with white waves far and nigh;
Level sand stretches as far as the boundless sky.
Waves never cease to wash from night till day,
Till the Eastern Sea turns into fields of clay.
I ask the river and sea, "Which is deeper, pray,
Your water or my longing night and day?
I hate you not so faithful as the tide,
For my longing is deeper than the sea wide."
Pan Zhengzheng

佛光顶上，阳光被佛光玉折为虹彩。一位禅师一半僧衣一半劲装，手持禅杖，静立如那诸佛造像中的一尊。 你听闻这位禅师早已易名北上，如今，却在此地意外相逢。禅师面具之下的脸波澜不惊，你只远远听得声如洪钟的询问：小施主，你是想见我的假相，法相，还是真相？……
#Y真相。你知他真相，知他如石如梅之骨，亦知他如火如月之心。此地唯有你们二人，便可显真相，交真心。#E
禅师并未回答，而是低声颂了句佛号。霎时间，你仿佛看到他身后狂风呼啸，一尊巨大的佛像显露出来。“纵观三相，不如无相。”耳边传来禅师低沉而洪亮的声音。他背后的巨佛像双手合十，风沙隐去了他的身形。待风沙散去，佛光顶上唯有日光彻地，虹彩依然，仿佛禅师从未出现。你不禁怀疑，方才那无相无定之人是否真的折返清河？还是自己这一程入梦又醒，自己产生了幻觉？
en:
Atop Halo Peak, sunlight fractured through the Buddha's Light Jade into drifting rainbow hues. There stood a Chan master, clad half in monk's robes and half in martial garb, Khakkhara staff in hand, as motionless as one of the myriad Buddha statues.
You had heard this master had long since changed his name and journeyed north, yet here, of all places, you unexpectedly crossed paths. His face beneath the mask was entirely unreadable; from afar, you only heard his voice, resonant as a temple bell, asking, "Young patron, do you wish to see my false form, my Dharma form, or my true form?"...
#YTrue form. You know his true form. You know the cast of his spirit, steadfast as stone, pure as winter plum, and his heart, bright as flame and clear as moonlight. Here, with only the two of you, he may at last reveal his true form and meet you with his true heart.#E
The master gave no answer, but murmured the Buddha's name under his breath. In that instant, howling winds seemed to surge behind him, and the silhouette of a colossal Buddha manifested. "To behold the three forms is not as profound as the formless," the master's low, sonorous voice echoed right beside your ear. Behind him, the great Buddha pressed its palms together, and wind and sand swallowed his form whole. When the wind and sand settled, only sunlight bathed Halo Peak. The rainbows remained unchanged, as if the Chan master had never been there at all. You could not help but wonder whether that formless, unbound man had truly returned to Qinghe. Or perhaps this whole journey had been no more than a dream, leaving you with nothing but a hallucination?

"月娘吾妻：

不知家中一切可好？爹的腿脚还疼吗，你的身子如何，霞儿可识字了？随军两年，只攒够了一封家书的钱粮，实我之过。

这几年辛苦月娘和爹打点家中，粮饷我都攒着，就等着带回来给你。你平常仔细着身子，莫要替我担忧。
"
"<信纸有火燎过的痕迹，有些字迹难以辨认>

绝笔信……至亲手中……

皇帝降了……将军降了……辽国大将…………杀……降兵……银鞍契丹……悉数被诛……
兄弟五人……当逃兵……身上粮饷……一分为五……与家书……送至家中……
若身死……信……焚之……不……祸家人。

诸兄弟籍贯、亲属如下
囗石   栾囗囗囗 囗囗城布坊，囗囗氏，弟赵铁。囗弟照顾好家母。
周富贵 清河囗囗 无亲眷。
李囗行 滹沱囗囗 荻花洲囗囗囗，父李阿公、嘱妻囗囗再嫁。
……
斡特剌 幽州人氏 爹娘弟兄囗囗囗死，囗妻囗囗梨朵，有孕囗囗，囗莫向北走，勿要回头，切记切记。"
en:
"My beloved wife Yueniang:

I wonder how everything is at home? Does Father's leg still hurt? How is your health? Has Xia'er learned to read? After two years with the army, I have only saved enough for one family letter. It is my fault.
But last year, I came to serve under General Zhao Dejun. Fortunately, I learned some characters from our father back then, and with the help of my brothers in the army, I was promoted to squad leader. Perhaps I can send a little more money home in the future. The soldiers under General Zhao are all very skilled. There is also a team of barbarian soldiers, all Khitans riding silver-saddled horses, fighting for us Han people. I learned some riding and archery from them. When I go to the battlefield and earn military merit, I might be able to come home and visit.

Thank you, Yueniang, and Father, for managing the household these past years. I have saved all my pay, waiting to bring it back to you. Take care of yourself, don't worry about me.
"
"<The letter paper shows signs of being burned. Some characters are illegible>

Last letter... to my family...

The Emperor has surrendered... the General has surrendered... the Liao general... kill... surrendered troops... the silver-saddled Khitans... all executed...
Five brothers... we will desert... divide our pay... into five parts... send with this letter... to our families...
If I die... burn this letter... don't... bring trouble to my family.

The brothers' registered origins and relatives are as follows: □ Shi Luan □□ □□ City Cloth Workshop, □□ Shi, younger brother Zhao Tie. □□ brother, take care of our mother. Zhou Fugui Qinghe □□ No relatives. Li □ Xing Hutuo □□ Reed Flower Islet □□ □, father Li Abo, instructs his wife □□ to remarry.
...
Wotela Youzhou native. Parents and brothers □□□□ dead. □ wife □□ Liduo, pregnant □□. □ do not go north, do not look back. Remember, remember."

zh:
萧史从萧府逃跑的那一刻，他看着前头救他的那位江湖人，后头是追来的家仆，笑了起来，风从他的耳边路过，衣摆被撞得作响，撞向风的人总有一种自由的错觉，他像是一只从笼子里飞出的鸟，这只鸟不往天空去，往江湖走。

他唯一停下来的瞬间，是在去江湖的路上，路过了沈府。

他不喜欢没有风的地方，但沈府摆明了是这样的地方，那位沈家小姐的后院，太过死气沉沉，他又回想起曾经见过的，那沈家小姐的模样，她看起来爱笑，但笑得从来不变，她看起来是好看的。
他再看一眼，却觉得她像个假人。
但他后来想明白了她像什么。像庭院里摆着的美轮美奂的假山，堂屋内放着的雕刻精致的玉石，一年四季不会凋零的假绒花，哪个达官显贵家内都想要摆上一座，但这些东西永远一层不变，一动不动。
人只会收藏一块玉石，不会爱上一块玉石。

他的印象太过深刻，以至于在这死气沉沉的院落和假山之间，本被他以为是与其类似的沈玉推开窗，脸上没有一丝笑模样，撒了谎，又随手用鸟食来逗他的瞬间，他愣了半晌。
然后那点活气对他下了逐客令，他在窗外呆了会儿，他弄不明白。
“她本来不是这样的。”

萧史想，那她本来应该怎么样的呢，像一座假山，还是一块玉石？
可她本来就是个人，她本来就应该是这样的，因为人不该像假山，不该像玉石，人应该像人。
但世上有很多人，不知道这一点。
en:
The moment Xiao Shi fled the Xiao estate, he looked ahead to the jianghu man helping him escape, and behind him to the servants chasing him, and he laughed. The wind rushed past his ears, his robes flaring wildly. There's a kind of illusion that comes with running into the wind, an illusion of freedom. He felt like a bird loosed from its cage. Not flying to the sky, but into the jianghu.

He only stopped once on the road to freedom by the Shen estate.

He disliked places where the wind didn't stir, and the Shen estate was clearly one of them. The rear courtyard where the Shen family's young lady resided was far too lifeless. He recalled the smile she always wore when they met, always the same, never changing. She was pretty, that he remembered. 

But the more he looked, the more she seemed... unreal.

Later, he realized what she reminded him of. Like the ornate rockeries set in noblemen's courtyards. Like the finely carved jade displayed in the great hall. Like the velvet blossoms that never wilt, no matter the season. Every wealthy household wanted one, but they were things that never changed, never moved.

People collect jade. But no one falls in love with it.

That impression stuck with him so strongly that when Shen Yu, whom he had always thought to be just like the lifeless stones and rockeries, suddenly opened her window without a smile, told a lie, and casually used birdseed to tease him, he froze.

That tiny spark of life in her cast him out. He stood outside her window for a long while, confused.

"She wasn't like this before," he thought.

But then, what was she supposed to be like? Like a rockery? Like a piece of jade?

No. She was a person. She was always supposed to be like this. Because people shouldn't be like rockeries. They shouldn't be like jade. People should be like people.

But too many in this world... don't know that.
Mei Yin Fan Qianhen

zh:
盖闻一日夫妻有百日之恩。
二娘有幸逢君，嘉礼初成于春和之日，良缘缔结及笄之期。
奈何钟鼎之家，一夕倾覆。本欲玉碎随君而去，却未想郎君修书逐妾于河西。
妾知郎君冷言放妻，实欲护妾周全。
此生难再遇君，唯有筚路蓝缕，于此绝境拼一丝生机，方不负郎君苦心。
纵观此生，妾纵横沙海，堪当大任。若泉下得见，定令君刮目。
此世缘浅，但求来生。妾无遗憾，愿君长知。
柳思安  拜别
en:
They say a single day as husband and wife fosters a hundred days of grace. I was truly fortunate to have met you, my lord, to be wed in the warmth of spring, our fates bound as I came of age.

Yet our noble house fell in a single night. I intended to follow you, to shatter like jade, but word came from Hexi that you had cast me aside.
I know too well that your cold words of release were a shield to grant me life.

In this life, we may never meet again. Therefore, I must blaze a trail through this wasteland, carving out a chance at survival from this utter despair. Only then can I honor the sacrifice you made for me.

Reflecting on this life, I have crossed seas of sand and shouldered great responsibilities. If we should meet again in the Yellow Springs, I swear you will see me with new eyes.

Our fate in this world was brief, yet I pray for the next. I hold no regrets. May you always know this.

A respectful farewell,
Liu Si'an

The street also holds fine treasures for it to carry off in its mouth, though it later discovered these were merely things dropped by the two-legged folk. Whenever a person recovered their treasure, they would cry "Thanks," and though the cat understood not the words, it took a liking to the phrase and claimed it as its own name. zh:
遍游皇城，我独在这福宁殿吃了个大亏！
我不过是好奇官家寝殿，才刚把脑袋探进去，就被一股浑厚内力震得倒退三尺，险些栽个仰面朝天！也不知是哪路大内高手在此坐镇，出手竟如此霸道？
又闻殿内卫士宫人蹴鞠较技、谈笑哗然之声，方探首向内一觑，却忽被莫名力道推搡，直摔得仰面朝天，险些撞及对面宫墙。也不知何方高手在此驻守，竟是这般暴性！
彼时身侧恰有一胖黄狗，咧嘴吐舌，瞥见我瘫地模样，竟还扭臀摇尾，大摇大摆钻入了殿门！
姑且记此一跤，来日再寻回颜面，定要将这福宁殿探个底朝天！
en:
Of all my wandering around the Imperial City, I took my worst tumble at Funing Hall. I was only curious about His Majesty's bedchamber. I had barely poked my head in when a surge of Inner Power slammed into me and sent me stumbling back three full paces. I nearly went flat on my back.
What kind of Imperial Master is posted here, to strike so brutally? I could even hear the guards and attendants inside, playing cuju and laughing up a storm. I leaned in for another peek, and that unseen force shoved me again, straight onto my back. I almost smashed into the wall opposite. Whoever's stationed here has a nasty temper.
And right then, a fat yellow dog waddled up beside me, tongue lolling. It took one look at me sprawled on the ground, wagged its tail, and swaggered right through the doors.
Fine. I'll remember this. One of these days I'll get my pride back and turn Funing Hall inside out.

Dear Brother Kongshan,

To avenge our master, I have hidden myself in Hearthfall Hamlet.
I heard you were running a noodle shop here. I wanted nothing more than to light a candle and talk with you through the night. However, I am currently disguised as a Xuanyuan disciple. Though we are mere steps apart, I dared not reveal myself, fearing it might jeopardize the plan.
Since I took up our late master's mantle as the head of Lone Cloud, we have been apart for far too long. If you are willing, come to the abandoned house next to your noodle shop tonight. I hide in the secret cellar beneath it.
Light the five bright lamps in the cellar, and the mechanism will open on its own. Then, at last, we can meet in the shadows.

zh:
是个晒谷不用翻的好天气。
方白在院里挥着笤帚，将被风吹散的麦穗轻轻聚拢。鸡崽子亦步亦趋地跟在帚后，争抢着翻飞的麦麸。

邻家婶子隔着篱笆扯闲天，说是风来了，天愈发要冷，话头三绕两绕，终究还是落在他身边没个知冷知热的人。
方白手下没停，笑着朝那群鸡崽努了努嘴：“我这儿‘家眷’可不少，日日吵得我头疼，若再添一位，怕是连这片刻清净也无了。哎哟，说得越发憋闷了，我得下地去透透气——”
话音未落，人已扛着锄头大步流星地出了院门，空留乡邻在原地摇头长叹。

地里的散碎麦粒藏得隐蔽，人眼难寻，倒是麻雀总知道去处。方白一面缓缓耕地，一面留心那些倏起倏落的身影。待麻雀落下，便走过去轻轻挥手，待鸟儿惊飞，才俯身拾起沾泥的麦粒，吹去浮土，仔细收进贴身的衣兜。

余闲圃最后两枚灯笼柿子又恰好被上一个人买走了，接连几天都是如此，方白喃喃道习惯了。
天色从浓郁的湛蓝过渡到绚烂的橙红，他呆呆看日暮西斜，虽抢不着灯笼柿子，至少没有错过晚霞间的天地。
痴望着天，竟不知走到哪处，落下一个柿子砸了头。熟得有些太透的柿子，沾得发丝也黏糊糊。
柿子捧在手心里，欲向谁诉说，抬头唯有一棵柿子树而已。

孤独幽幽地徘徊，他想着为自己写的志怪篇章添个尾巴。那故事写了只毛发苍黄的灵兽，堕了犬胎，得一贱名阿黄，却还惦记自己是头狮子。虽形骸困于家圃，却行为殊异，不逐猫兔，不食残羹，不尽犬职，终被天雷打死。
回到家院石桌，墨痕间还沾着鸡雏们啄剩的麦糠。方白捻起一粒渣，忽有所感，重又提笔。阿黄残魂未泯之际，群禽衔露，羽庇其身，如行往生法事。至此金身化去，轻烟融入晓雾之中。
这被家禽环绕的，平静而温煦的终结，似乎……也并不坏。

远远的，只听一团年轻人嚷着什么。走近些看，这些人衣衫不整，手握舆图，神色惘然。白衣上染泥的染泥，沾灰的沾灰。
方白正欲调笑，却对上了那五人呆愣愣的眼神。几个没头没脑的小青年见了方白，眼儿齐刷刷地一亮，你扯我追地扑腾着，好容易赶上前来，却又摔作一团。
“师叔！方师叔！您就是方师叔吧！”
方白见着衣衫样式，早就心里有数。只是故作嫌弃：“我那好师兄，收的弟子怎么越发像呆瓜了？”
青年竟痛哭起来。那些眼泪，令人不安。染就那片橙红天的，是一轮近血色的夕阳。
“师叔……我们文津馆……没了……”

风的确来了。天，愈发要冷。
en:
A fine day for drying grain, the kind where you don't even have to turn it.
In the courtyard, Fang Bai gently swept, gathering stray wheat ears scattered by the breeze. The chicks followed at his heels, scrambling for the drifting chaff kicked up by the broom.
Across the fence, the neighbor's wife called out, chatting warmly but with a hint of warning that the wind's arrival would only make the days colder. Her words meandered, but the talk always drifted back to the fact that he had no soul to keep him warm.

Without missing a beat, Fang kept sweeping, a playful smile tugging at his lips as he nudged the chicks with his foot. "I've got plenty of ‘kin' here, squawking and fussing every day. What a headache. Add one more to the mix, and there'd be no peace left at all. Ah, maybe I should head out to the fields and breathe some fresh air."
He shouldered his hoe and made a swift exit, leaving the neighbors behind, shaking their heads with quiet sighs.

The scattered grains hidden among the furrows were nearly invisible to the human eye, but the sparrows always knew where to find them. As Fang worked the land slowly, he kept an eye on the lively birds flitting to and fro. Whenever one settled nearby, he'd gently wave a hand, sending it fluttering away. Only when they took flight would he stoop to gather the muddied grains, blowing off the dust before tucking them carefully into his pocket.

The last two Lantern Persimmons in the Leisure Garden had just been sold. This same scene has played out for days on end. Fang had grown used to it.
The sky shifted from a deep, velvety blue to a brilliant blaze of orange and crimson as he stared silently at the setting sun sinking behind the hills. Though he missed out on the persimmons, he caught a glimpse of the breathtaking evening glow stretching across the earth.
Lost in the quiet beauty of the dusk, he wandered without noticing where he'd gone until suddenly, a ripe persimmon dropped down, thudding softly against his head. The fruit was overripe, a sticky mess that matted his hair. He cupped the fruit in his hands, searching silently for someone to share this simple moment.
But all that greeted him was the quiet, solitary persimmon tree standing tall against the fading light.

A quiet loneliness drifted with him as he pondered adding an epilogue to the strange tale he'd been weaving. The story told of a spirit beast, its fur faded to a weary yellow, cast into a dog's womb and given the lowly name "Ahuang," yet it never forgot it was born a lion. Though its bones were trapped in a domestic yard, its behavior set it apart: it neither chased cats nor hares, refused scraps and leftovers, shirked its canine duties until at last, it was struck dead by celestial thunder.

Back at the stone table in his courtyard, ink stains still mingled with fallen grains of wheat that the chicks had left behind. Fang pinched a stray husk between his fingers. Moved by a sudden spark, he took up his brush once more. As Ahuang's remnant soul flickered, birds brought dew and shielded the dog with feathers, as if performing a rite of rebirth. In that moment, Ahuang's golden form dissolved into wisps of smoke, blending softly into the morning mist. Such a peaceful, tender farewell, surrounded by the warmth of those feathered companions, seemed... not so bad after all.

From afar, the clamor of a pack of youngsters broke the air. Their white robes were caked with mud and choked with dust. They clutched maps, their faces an unreadable mix of confusion and hope.
Fang was ready with a quip, but then he caught the vacant, shell-shocked stares in their eyes. The ragged youths' faces brightened suddenly, scrambling and tripping over one another, only to tumble into a heap at his feet.

"Master Fang! Uncle Fang! You're Master Fang, aren't you?"
As he recognized their attire, Fang Bai's heart tightened, though he feigned a gruff rebuke. "My dear Senior Brother... has he started recruiting nothing but airheads these days?"
Then the floodgates broke. Those tears... they were unsettling. The orange sky was now bled through by a sun the color of gore.
"Master... our Inkbound Order... it's gone..."
The wind had truly arrived. And it was only going to get colder.

zh: 建安七子之冠冕王粲，避乱荆州，依刘表而无所用，登当阳城楼，感慨而作此赋。此赋被收入南朝梁昭明太子所编之《文选》，列为赋类“游览”之首，历代传诵。其“怀土怀才、两相纠缠”之旨，为后世言“登高而赋”者开一法门，今之文人，尤重其慷慨悲凉之气。
en: Wang Can, foremost among the Seven Masters of Jian'an, fled the turmoil of the age to Jingzhou, where he found shelter under Liu Biao yet was given no office to fulfill his talents. Ascending the tower at Dangyang, he was moved to compose this rhapsody. It was gathered into the Selections of Refined Literature, the literary anthology compiled by Crown Prince Zhaoming of the Liang dynasty in the Southern Courts, where it stands at the head of the Journey and Sightseeing division of the rhapsody section, recited and admired across the ages ever since. Its guiding spirit—the longing for one's homeland and the longing to serve, the two intertwined without resolution—opened a gate for all later writers who would ascend to great heights and give voice to their sorrows in verse. Scholars of letters today hold in particular esteem the air of stirring melancholy that pervades it.

Stay warm, fed, and safe out there.

zh:
沉疴久矣，命数所尽，天难救我，唯有三问不明。

一问与亲。您幼时论兵讲剑，蕴习武经，得孙武白起之精，见韬钤之骨髓。待年少之时，观荧惑而芒衰，知吐蕃之运尽。誓心归国，决意无疑，咸通八年，父亲身死，您束身归阙，命葬他乡，托人相问，只得一言，言您有时而无命，得遇梦奠之灾。早知今日，您亦束手？

二问与君。我辈将大唐置于心，唐既于我心，怎不见我辈肺腑，不见我辈赤胆，今朝陨命，淮深唯恨战未平，恨天时杀我，人和断我，刀戈向我，杀我辈者，为何竟是自肚腹而出？

三问与己。此生今日，乌护噬我，竖子断我，大唐弃我，妻儿殒命，幼子何辜？淮深环顾此生，不知何罪至此?

#N淮深无罪，无罪之人，不当束手。#E
en:
My long illness will soon claim me, beyond even heaven's saving. Yet three questions still puzzle me.

First, to my uncle. In youth, you mastered the military canon and grasped the essence of tactics. By reading the stars, you foresaw that Tubo Kingdom's fortune was waning. You vowed to return to the homeland with unwavering resolve. When my father died, you gave yourself to the throne. They kept you there until the end and buried you far from home. All you left me were these words: "My moment would come, but I would not live to see it.“ You knew all along, and still you submitted?

Second, to my Emperor. In our hearts we upheld the Tang. Yet, our devotion and loyalty went unseen. My only regret is that the war is not yet won. Fate failed me, and men betrayed me. But why must the knife in the back come from my own kin?!

Third, to myself. Oghuz have devoured me, traitors have betrayed me, the Tang have abandoned me... What sin did I commit to deserve this?

#NI am innocent, and an innocent man does not submit!#E

锦缎是原本的质地，旧是过往历经的岁月。
父亲把这双鞋送出的时候，在鞋尖上缀上了两颗夜明珠。
那是权臣给这位江湖侠客的见面礼。

惊涛掌未曾收过这么重的礼，左思右想，最后把这珠子缀在了给女儿的新鞋上。
但兰澳扯掉了明珠，将那华贵的珠宝丢了出去，珠子咕噜噜滚过客栈油腻腻的过道，依然不改它的明光。
无论是糊里糊涂收下礼物的父亲，还是不明所以但是就是不喜欢的女儿，
那时候他们都不知道，上位者所有的馈赠，都会让你付出昂贵的代价。或早或晚。
en:
A pair of old brocade shoes. 

The brocade recalls what they were made to be, and the wear tells the story of all the years they've traveled through. 
When the father gifted these shoes, he attached two glowing pearls to the toes— 
gifts from a powerful noble to a wanderer. 

Palm Strike Master had never received such a lavish present before. After much thought, he fastened the pearls to a new pair intended for his daughter. 
But Lan Ao tore them away, tossing the precious jewels to the dusty floor, where they rolled across the greasy inn hallway, still shining with unyielding light. 
Neither the bewildered father who accepted the gift, nor the daughter who rejected it, 
understood then that such favors from the mighty always came with a hidden price—one paid sooner or later.

zh:
这地方每道门差别不大，顶多是紫藤花架与玉兰花树的区别，只有一处的布料架子比屋顶都高，铺满了彩布和金纱，日头一照，像被风吹起的酒旗，老远就能瞧见。既然如此醒目，便先记这一笔。
走近了才发觉，布匹高架旁边的树开满了花，我方才竟没注意——应当是那染色的布帛太过耀眼，简直像九天落下的虹彩，把花色都比下去了。
每抬悬挂布帛的架子下头都有宫人忙碌。身量还没布匹宽，手里的活儿却没停过，汗珠子滚下来也来不及擦，就这么滴进染缸里，和斑斓的颜料混在一起……这满宫的锦绣，到底要多少汗水才染得完？
再抬头看向那布帛，我忽然不再觉得虹彩美丽了。
en:
At first glance, the gates here all look much the same, differing only in details, a wisteria trellis here, a magnolia tree there. Only one place stood out. The racks rose higher than the roofs themselves, draped with bright silks and gold brocade. When the sun hits them, they look like tavern flags snapping in the wind, so striking you can spot them from far off. I had to make note of it.
Only when I got closer did I realize the trees beside the tall racks were covered in blossoms. I had missed them at first, dazzled by the dyed fabric, like a rainbow spilled from the heavens, outshining the flowers.
Beneath the racks, palace workers hurried back and forth. They looked smaller than the bolts they were working, but their hands never stopped. Sweat ran down their faces, dripping into the dye vats before they could even wipe it away, mixing with those brilliant colors. All the splendor in this palace, how much sweat does it take to dye it all? When I looked up at those lengths of fabric again, they no longer seemed so beautiful.

zh:

数载后，天下毒虫大半已去，惟一蟾妖藏于毒渊。仙人入渊以长生明灯镇妖，灯灭影现，山裂泉涌。蟾妖永镇荧渊，仙人亦大道圆满，飞升而去。
群侠感念此事，著《长生仙人传》，百姓亦于朔望之日持灯拜北斗，铭恩仙人。
颂曰：「负罪迎神，得见长生。」
en:
In the age of chaos after the Liang Dynasty fell, warlords vied for supremacy. So great was the slaughter that rivers were choked with bones, and plague-bearing vermin festered across the land.

A fellowship of heroes begged an immortal for aid. To show their unwavering resolve, the immortal laughed, destroyed their own mountain grotto, and strode forth to join the cause.

Years later, the land was cleansed, save for a single great toad demon lurking in the Poison Abyss. The immortal descended into the depths, bearing the Ever-burning Lamp to suppress the beast. At the climax of their battle, the lamp was extinguished. In its place, a brilliant silhouette appeared as the very mountain shattered and a pure spring erupted forth. The demon was sealed forever in the abyss, which, purified by the sacrifice, was henceforth known as the Gleaming Abyss.

Having perfected their path, the immortal ascended to the heavens. And in eternal gratitude, the heroes chronicled the epic in the Tales of Immortals. To this day, the common folk honor the sacrifice by lighting lamps and praying to the Northern Dipper on the new and full moons.

An ode commemorates the immortal's lesson: Only through worship can one glimpse immortality.

自碧水云涛一别后，你不时会收到少年三杰从墨城寄来的信件。
——大侠，你怎么还不来找我们玩啊？
——大侠大侠，山里的云槎修到哪啦？你什么时候再带我们坐坐呀？
当然，孩子们最常问起的，还是鸦先生的“种子”，
——种子到底在哪里呀？
——种子长大了吗？
——种子长得好吗？
……
你写下回信：
#Y【种子长高了。】你们想必也长高了一大截吧！许久未见，得空了定来找你们玩。#E
寄出信件之后，你寻空来到墨城，接上期盼已久的孩子们，又一次坐上建好轨道的云槎，重回碧云水涛。
种子在金灿灿的稻田里，在漫天花雨的桃林中，在淙淙的流水里……种子长得很好很好。
en:
Since parting ways at Jadestream Valley, you have frequently received letters from the Three Junior Paragons of Mohist City.
"Great Wanderer, why haven't you come to play with us yet?"
"Great Wanderer! How's the Sky Shuttle in the mountains coming along? When can you take us for another ride?"
But above all, they pester about Master Raven's "seeds."
"Where on earth are the seeds?"
"Have the seeds grown up yet?"
"Are the seeds doing well?"
...
You sit down to write back:
#Y[The seeds have grown taller.] I bet you all have shot up quite a bit, too! It's been a while since we last met; I'll surely visit you when I have the time.#E
After sending the letter, you visit Mohist City. You pick up the long-awaiting children and board the Sky Shuttle once more, gliding along the completed tracks back to Jadestream Valley.
The seeds are in the golden rice paddies, amidst the falling petals of Peach Grove, and within the gurgling brooks... The seeds are growing very, very well.
...Harsh, but not wrong.

zh:
盛夏至，病者日增，应接不暇。青溪诸大夫乃汇近日出诊所得于《伤热杂病论》，以济众人。

——正文——

急火攻心之为病：梨园者中暑遭鹅，逐而啄之，愤而作剧，誓曰血溅白练、三年大汗、六月飞雪。冷静汤主之。

人祸之为病：文津馆舍友闭户，不启窗，五人气蒸。开窗散主之。（互踢主之，亦可。）

食炙之为病：孤云者暑食烤鸡烤兔，腹热便结，唇裂口干。凉拌瓜齑主之。（若仍欲烤，先服苦参汤，自悔则止。）

贪冰之为病：日啖冰数杯，饮多则胃寒肠鸣。姜枣汤主之。（医者告曰：冰可缓，不可贪。）

湿温之为病：长夏湿热交蒸，头痛恶寒，身重疼痛，胸闷不饥，状若阴虚。三仁汤主之。

青溪大夫合告曰，防暑于未然，药补不如食补。绿豆解暑，甜瓜生津，姜枣暖胃。正确防暑，从今日始。
en:
As high summer arrived, the sick grew ever more numerous, more than could be attended to. And so the physicians of Silver Needle gathered the findings of their recent house calls into the "Treatise on Heat Damage," that all might be aided.

- Main Text -

On the ailment of sudden fire assaulting the heart: A disciple of the Masked Troupe, overcome by heat, was set upon by a goose which chased and pecked at him; in his fury he composed a drama, swearing an oath of blood spattered on white feather, three years of great sweating, and snow falling in the sixth month. This is treated by Calming Decoction.

On the ailment of man-made calamity: Roommates of Inkbound Order shut their doors and would not open the windows, and five men steamed together in the close air. This is treated by Window-Opening Dispersal. (Mutual Kicking may also serve.)

On the ailment of roasted foods: A disciple of Lone Cloud ate roasted chicken and roasted rabbit in the heat of summer, whereupon his belly grew hot and bound, his lips cracked, and his mouth ran dry. This is treated by Cold-Dressed Melon Relish. (Should he still desire to roast more, let him first take Bitter Sophora Decoction, and cease once regret sets in.)

On the ailment of greed for ice: One who eats several cups of ice daily, and drinks overmuch, shall find his stomach chilled and his bowels rumbling. This is treated by Ginger-Jujube Decoction. (The physician advises: ice may be taken in moderation, but never in excess.)

On the ailment of damp-heat: In the long summer, dampness and heat steam together, bringing headache and aversion to cold, heaviness and aching of the body, tightness in the chest without hunger, resembling a deficiency of yin. This is treated by Three-Kernel Decoction.

The physicians of Silver Needle jointly declare: it is better to guard against the heat before it strikes, and dietary nourishment surpasses medicinal supplement. Mung beans dispel the heat, sweet melon generates fluids, and ginger and jujube warm the stomach. Let proper heat prevention begin from this very day.

发现于：地字三左间

从一座空墓中掘出的短刃，柄上缠着褪色的红绳。
墓主的武功秘籍堆叠如小山，每一册扉页上都用狂躁的字迹反复写着同一个女人的名字——以及“烦死了”“可恨”之类的随笔。
那个叫狐令飞的墓主，生前自认傲视江湖，却唯独在这几行字里露出了败相。
阿狄学了几本武功，又割下其中一页，将它塞进怀中最贴身的位置。
撞见了如此奇遇的他毅然攥着匕首走出荒山。
他想，既然那个女人曾令狐令飞如此不甘，那么被关在岱山的她——或许缺一个徒弟。
一个像他这样的徒弟。
en:
Found in: Room Earth III Left

A dagger unearthed from an empty tomb, its hilt bound with faded red cord.

The tomb owner's martial manuals were stacked like a hill, every title page frantically scrawled with the same woman's name alongside agitated scribbles like "so annoying" and "damn it." Hu Lingfei, the master buried here, believed himself peerless in the martial world, yet these scattered words betrayed his defeat.
Di studied several manuals, sliced out a single page, and tucked it close against his chest.
Clenching the dagger, he strode out of the barren hills. If that woman had left Hu Lingfei so full of resentment, then perhaps she, currently imprisoned in Mount Tai, was in need of a disciple.
A disciple like him.

它在等，等一日春风吹散黄沙，毛球飞入天际——长安的柳絮飘飘，少女是不是就会笑了？
玉团儿低头舔了舔爪子，吐出一团又一团毛球。
en:
Fur Ball coughed up its furballs. 
The first clogged its throat, and it darted out from a crimson lacquered box, while the young girl inside hid her face. Fur Ball arched its back and spat out a soft tuft of snow-white fur. 
The second furball was damp and heavy. The girl was carried back to her tent—alive, but tasting of salt and sorrow. Fur Ball licked the corner of its mouth and spat out another tuft of white fluff. 
The third tangled with sand. The fourth tinged with blood. The fifth dissolved into the snow... Fur Ball carefully hid each one, tenderly guarding every fragile plume. 
It waited patiently for the spring winds to lift the desert dust and those furballs, like drifting willow fluff across the sky, like those floated over Chang'an. Would the girl's smile finally return? 
Fur Ball bowed its head, licked its paw, and spat out one more silky furball. And then another. And another still.

In their toughest days, it was the kindness of their neighbors that got them through. As time passed, Niu Mang's son, Niu Ben, grew up and started a small business on South Gate Avenue. Life got better, and he brought his father to live with him. But after a while, Niu Mang found himself missing the hustle and bustle of the old neighborhood—the noisy crowds, the ill-fed children with bright smiles, all the little things that made that place feel like home. zh:
小张将军的名头请不动我，但他说要补的剑是破白，所以我来了。 
等到炉子都烧红了，破白的主人都还没来。我把目光投向端坐的年轻人，迟迟没有将破白喂入火舌。 
师傅，不用等了，叔父他不会来了。 
是这次不来，还是以后都不会来？ 
铸剑室里只有破白被火焰炙烤的声音，像是给两张嘴封了烙印。我忘了，面前人不是我的恩人，只是破白的新主人。 
若他不要这把剑，凭什么不送还给我？我越想越气闷，把锤子往旁边一放，坐在地上瞪着年轻人。他为什么不来，是胳膊断了，拿不动剑了么？ 
……有人不让他拿剑，他只好把剑托给我，让我替他拿。 
我气得吹胡子瞪眼。铸剑的还在这里等着，拿剑的却跑了。人老了受了气，身子反倒利索，没过几日我便把破白给了小张将军，背起包袱走了。 
什么圣人都不能阻止他拿剑。只有握紧剑，才能杀了不让拿剑的人。 
等到了长安，我给他一把比破白更好的剑，让他接着做最威风的大将军……
en:
The title of Young General Zhang couldn't persuade me to come. But when he said the sword to be repaired was Palebreak, I came.  
The furnace was red-hot, but Palebreak's owner hadn't arrived. I looked at the young man sitting quietly, hesitating to feed Palebreak into the flames.  
Master, no need to wait. My uncle will not come.  
Not coming this time, or never coming again?  
The only sound in the forging room was Palebreak being scorched by the flames, as if sealing both our lips. I'd forgotten: the man in front of me wasn't my benefactor, just Palebreak's new owner.  
"If he doesn't want this sword, why not return it to me?" I grew more and more annoyed, putting down my hammer and sitting on the ground, staring at the young man. "Why isn't he coming? Did he break his arm and can't hold a sword anymore?"  
...Someone won't let him hold a sword. He had to entrust it to me, to hold it for him.  
I fumed, my beard bristling. "The swordsmith still waits here, yet the sword-wielder has fled." Old and provoked, my body became agile instead. Within a few days, I gave Palebreak to Young General Zhang, shouldered my pack, and left.  
No sage can stop him from holding a sword. Only by gripping the sword can he kill those who forbid him from holding it  
When I reach Chang'an, I'll give him a sword better than Palebreak, let him continue being the most awe-inspiring great general..

zh:
曹家的小娘子跟观音菩萨有大缘分呢。 
她自小就听人这么说。这说法最开始是从祖母常去祭拜的寺里传出来的。她年幼时长相讨喜，俨然一尊粉妆玉砌的玉雕娃娃，只是常常生病，一年到头竟没几日能下地的。祖母为她操碎了心，一遍一遍往寺里跑，诸天神佛都求遍了。直到一日，祖母带着她求到观音菩萨面前，刚磕完头，便有一陌生师太从观音像后面转出，拿杨柳枝在她眉心一点，随即施施然离去了。因这变故来的突然，佛堂中人都愣住了，直到那师太走出门后才想起追上去。果不其然，门外空无一人。自那之后，她的身体便一日日好了起来。寺里的法师说，她原是观音菩萨座下一尊玉雕童子投胎，因着原身是玉，天生无血无肉，所以借父母精血好得一身血肉，是要较常人虚弱些。这不，菩萨特来护她呢。又说她名中最好带上“观音”二字，好教各路小鬼知道她有菩萨看着，不敢近身。祖母将寺中人的话一一都听进去了，逐条照办，金身也塑了，玉雕也塑了，又请主持和法师们为她更名，大箱大箱的香火钱送进寺里……凉州的其他家族听闻这段佳话后也啧啧称奇，纷纷前来参拜，于是寺中香火日盛。 
佳话的主人倒是对此不甚上心。佛寺想要在凉州大族的圈子中站稳脚跟，需得有个噱头；年幼体弱的孩子并不少见，长长就好了；曹家要想在众家族中脱颖而出，也需做出一些姿态来造势，教人知道曹家一心向佛别无他心；至于那寒冬里鲜嫩的杨柳枝和面生的师太……大家都需要一个故事，戏法便成真的了。心自在笑她故作清醒，打趣她真真是玉石投胎。玉石就玉石吧，她或许的确生来有几分寒凉，得了神佛的恩惠也还是不信那些虚无缥缈的东西。所以她在寺中一遍遍抄经时，从没求过菩萨阻止这门婚事。她不求神佛，只求自己。 
菩萨啊，我错了。 
白玉雕似得观音急切地在神通册子背面写下一行字。她的眼泪还没流出来，就被高塔上呼啸的寒风吹干了。 
若我真是菩萨座下的玉石投胎，求您再看看我，看看我的琉璃吧。求您把她带回我身边……她还不知道，我写了什么啊……
en:
The young lady of the Cao family has a great affinity with Goddess of Mercy. 
She's heard this since childhood. The story first came from the temple her grandmother frequented. As a child, she was adorable, like a pink-and-white jade-carved doll, but often sick, barely able to leave her bed for more than a few days a year. Grandmother worried herself sick, running to the temple time and again, beseeching all deities. One day, Grandmother took her to pray before Goddess of Mercy. Just after they kowtowed, an unfamiliar nun emerged from behind the statue, touched her forehead with a willow branch, and then departed gracefully. The suddenness stunned everyone in the hall, only after the nun left did they think to follow. Sure enough, outside there was no one. From then on, her health gradually improved. The temple's master said she was originally a jade-carved acolyte under Goddess of Mercy reborn. Since her original form was jade, bloodless and fleshless, borrowing her parents' essence to gain a body made her naturally weaker than others. Thus, the Goddess of Mercy came specially to protect her. He also said it was best to include Goddess of Mercy in her name, so all minor ghosts would know she was watched by the Goddess of Mercy and dare not approach. Grandmother took every word to heart, complied item by item, commissioned golden statues, jade carvings, requested the abbot and masters to rename her, sent chests of offerings to the temple... Other Liangzhou families, hearing this tale, marveled and came to pay respects, so the temple's incense thrived. 
The subject of this tale was not much concerned. For a Buddhist temple to gain footing among Liangzhou's great families, it needed a hook. Sickly young children weren't rare, they often outgrew it. For the Cao family to stand out among the clans, they needed to make gestures to build momentum, show their single-minded devotion to Buddha. As for the fresh willow branch in deep winter and the unfamiliar nun... everyone needed a story, so the trick became truth. Xinzizai laughed at her for feigning clarity, teased that she really was jade reborn. So be it, jade reincarnation. Perhaps she was indeed born with a certain chill. Even having received divine grace, she still didn't believe in those ethereal things. So when she copied sutras in the temple, time and again, she never asked the Bodhisattva to stop the marriage. She did not beg gods or Buddhas, only relied on herself. 
Bodhisattva, I was wrong. 
The Goddess of Mercy, white as carved jade, hastily wrote a line on the back of her divine arts booklet. Her tears had not yet fallen before they were dried by the howling cold wind atop the high tower. 
If I am truly jade reborn under your seat, I beg you look upon me again, look upon my Liuli. Please bring her back to me... She doesn't even know what I've written...

唐末以来，兵乱相继，为充国库，赋税繁重，致耕者不敢勤于劳作，更无力开垦荒田。赋役相循，百姓生业，每况愈下。
然今天下已定，陛下爱民，厉行节约，敦本抑末，使百姓得以安养，使汴京市井繁荣，足见陛下良策成效。
民虽居草野，仍常闻民生多艰，故陈策二端：
于民，可令能广植桑枣、开荒田者，只纳旧租，永不通检，以劝耕织；
于州县官吏，可嘉奖能招复逋逃，劝课栽植者，使旷土得耕，游民得业。
en:
Since the late Tang, war and disorder have followed one upon another. To fill the coffers, taxes grew ever heavier, until those who tilled the land no longer dared labor in earnest, much less reclaim wasteland. Tax and corvée came one after the next, and the people's livelihood worsened by the day.
Yet now the realm has been brought to order. Your Majesty cherishes the people, practices frugality, and honors the root while restraining the secondary. Thus the people may live in peace, and the markets of Kaifeng flourish. This is proof enough of the success of Your Majesty's rule.
Though I dwell far from court, I still often hear of the hardships of common life. I therefore venture to submit two humble proposals:
For the people, let those who plant mulberry and jujube in abundance, or reclaim wasteland, pay only their former tax and never be reassessed thereafter, so as to encourage farming and sericulture.
For prefectural and county officials, let those who can call back runaways and fugitives, and promote cultivation and planting, be rewarded, so that abandoned land may be tilled again and the displaced regain their livelihood.

每件已穿戴装备使非风云际会弈子获得的属性幅度：50%→75%。
魁首提供给非风云际会弈子属性幅度：50%→75%。

新增三个全新变数：登天无返、印印不绝、飞来横财
#Y身份靠自己#E
增加的联结的计数目前已在变数详情弹窗中显示。

修复了前尘旧物浑铁重枪·青非普通攻击也能造成眩晕的问题。
修复了部分设备分屏后显示全屏，界面信息显示错误的问题。
en:
Wanderers, Jianghu Tactics welcomes "Grand Destiny" and balance adjustments for select synergies and pieces. Detailed updates are as follows:
#Y"New Mechanism"#E
The board resets as the divine Dao shifts. Jianghu Chess unveils Grand Destiny, where destiny favors both sides equally. At the start of every match, 1 of 28 unique Destinies manifests. Read the secret mechanisms, seize the momentum, and turn the tide!
#Y"Matchmaking Rules"#E
Matchmaking tier gap restriction in Ranked Mode: Adjusted from a 3-tier gap to a 6-tier gap eligible for matchmaking.
#Y"Chess Piece Adjustments"#E
#YBell Toller#E
Max Heroic Spirit: 100 → 90
#YZheng E#E
HP: 1576 → 1776
#YFeng Jisheng#E
Critical DMG: 140% → 120%
#YRaven#E
Initial Heroic Spirit of Raven: 20 → 0
#Y"Synergy Adjustments"#E
#YRuin's Glee#E
Tier 1 Synergy: At 40 or higher Pleasure Points, the attribute reduction (ATK, DEF, HP) for resurrected Ruin's Glee pieces is adjusted: 30% → 10%
#YKaifeng Feud#E
Tier 1 Synergy: Low-HP threshold for HP recovery on Kaifeng Feud pieces: 75% → 60%; HP recovery amount: 25% → 40%
#YRogue Champ#E
Attribute gain granted to non-Rogue Champ pieces per equipped gear piece: 50% → 75%.
Attribute gain provided by the Champion to non-Influential Gathering pieces: 50% → 75%.
Adjusted the Antiques automatically replaced by piece Guo Xin under the Tier 4 effect of Influential Gathering.
#Y"Variable Adjustments"#E
Added three brand-new Variables: One-Way Ascent, Endless Seals, Windfall.
#YSelf-Made Status#E
Added Synergy counter counts are now displayed in the Variable details pop-up window.
#YCentral Command I and Central Command#E
Added active piece names to the display in the Variable details popup window.
#Y"Optimizations & Fixes"#E
Optimized matchmaking rules for the final 3 remaining players to avoid accidentally matching against the same opponent consecutively.
Optimized piece skill casting logic, fixing an issue where certain pieces with full Heroic Spirit would cast skills into empty space.
Fixed an issue where the extra Champion selected via the Duel of Heroes Variable displayed incorrectly.
Fixed an issue where Shield Values provided by the Antiques of Liu Qingyi: Everlasting Lock and Lie Yan: Yanyun Armor were not affected by piece attributes.
Fixed an issue where the Antiques: Heavy Iron Spear: Halcyon caused Stun on non-Normal Attacks.
Fixed an issue where split-screen displays forced into fullscreen on certain devices caused interface information display errors.

每局获得定量#Y铜钱#E，按购物清单购入所需货物，所购皆入#Y背篓#E，容量有限。完成清单为基本条件，余钱可继续采买提升得分，结算时#Y优先对比清单完成个数次对比分数#E进行排名区分。#Y道具品质越高分值越高#E。
所有摊位#Y库存共享#E，他人买走即少一件。摊位售空后将#Y自动补货#E，但#Y补货价高于原价#E，先到先得更为划算。
背篓中多余货物可由#Y替役贩#E低价回收，回笼铜钱灵活运转。
集市中不时触发摊位事件：
#Y削价#E——限时降价，可省铜钱。
#Y大派送#E——摊主低价甩卖，机不可失。
#Y现做#E——需等候制作方可购买，售空不会自动补货。
#Y扫荡#E——他人抢购，库存骤减，宜速取之。
抢占货物、善用事件时机、合理规划路线，#Y满足通关条件时，得分越高排名越前#E。
en:
Multiple players compete in the same arena, shopping against the clock and fighting over limited goods.
Each round grants a fixed amount of #YCopper Coin#E. Purchase the required goods according to the shopping list; all purchases go into your #YBackpack#E, which has limited capacity. Completing the list is the basic requirement. Any remaining money can be spent on more purchases to raise your score. At settlement, rankings are determined by #Yfirst comparing the number of list items completed, then comparing scores#E. #YHigher-quality items are worth more points#E.
All stalls #Yshare inventory#E; when another player buys an item, one less remains. Sold-out stalls will #Yrestock automatically#E, but #Yrestock prices are higher than original prices#E, so arriving first is more cost-effective.
Excess goods in your Backpack can be sold cheaply to the #YLabor Broker#E to recoup Copper Coins for later use.
Stall events may trigger in the market:
#YPrice Cut#E: limited-time discount that saves Copper Coins.
#YGrand Giveaway#E: stall owner clears goods at low prices. Do not miss it.
#YMade to Order#E: you must wait for production before purchasing. Sold-out items will not restock automatically.
#YSweep#E: others rush to buy, causing inventory to drop sharply. Act fast.
Seize goods, take advantage of events, and plan your route carefully. #YOnce clear conditions are met, the higher your score, the higher your rank#E.

zh: 《春秋公羊传》成于战国至汉初。春秋三传之一，《春秋》经传初各单行，后人割传附经，遂成今本。相传为公羊高受学于子夏，口说流传，至汉景帝时，其玄孙公羊寿与弟子胡毋生著于竹帛，遂成定本。全书以阐发《春秋》微言大义为主，其学重在义理，尤重义例，善从经文褒贬中推求圣人之意。汉初将其立为官学，设博士，董仲舒以《公羊》说灾异、论天人，著《春秋繁露》，公孙弘以《公羊》起白衣至丞相，于是其学大行于世。东汉何休作《春秋公羊解诂》，集两汉公羊学之大成，其义例精密，为传世最重要之注本。唐徐彦据何注作疏，题为《春秋公羊传注疏》，列入官学。
en: Gongyang Zhuan was completed between the Warring States period and the early Han dynasty. It is one of the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals. The canon and commentary originally circulated separately; later scholars divided the commentary and appended it to the canon, thus producing the text as it stands today. It is said that Gongyang Gao received learning from Zixia, and the teaching was transmitted orally through the generations until, in the reign of Emperor Jing of Han, his great-great-grandson Gongyang Shou, together with his disciple Hu Wusheng, committed it to bamboo and silk, thus establishing the definitive text. The work is devoted chiefly to expounding the subtle words and profound meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Its learning places foremost emphasis on righteousness and principle, and in particular on the precedents of righteousness, drawing from the praise and censure within the canon to seek out the intent of the Sages. In the early Han it was established among the official academies, and a designated Scholar post was created for it. Dong Zhongshu employed Gongyang Zhuan to discourse on portents and calamities and to deliberate on the relations between Heaven and Man, composing the Luxuriant Dew of the Spring and Autumn Annals; Gongsun Hong rose by means of Gongyang Zhuan from a commoner to the office of Chief Minister, and thus its learning spread greatly through the world. In the Eastern Han, He Xiu composed the Interpretation and Explication of Gongyang Zhuan, gathering the full achievement of Gongyang learning across the two Han dynasties; its precedents of righteousness are meticulous, making it the most important annotated edition transmitted to posterity. In the Tang, Xu Yan composed a subcommentary based on He Xiu's annotations, entitled the Annotated Subcommentary on Gongyang Zhuan, and it was incorporated into the official academies.

After three months, he finally mastered the eighteen techniques. Later, he further integrated them into martial arts, creating what he passed down to his disciples as "Skygrasp Rope Dart", which is a method meant not only to scale the heights of Taihang but also to reach for the heavens for all living beings.
